radio, Step 2: Alternatives Now that you've defined the parameters and primed the AI with relevant knowledge, let's move on to Alternatives. This step is all about exploring diverse perspectives and approaches. Instead of focusing solely on the actions you took or the solutions you came up with, challenge the AI to generate alternative approaches. In the customer churn example, you might ask the AI, "Can you suggest different analytical techniques or models that could provide new insights into churn?" Encourage the AI to actively participate in this exploration by asking it if it has any questions about the situation or the desired outcome. This helps uncover knowledge gaps and ensures a more thorough understanding of the topic. For example, you might ask the AI, "Do you have any questions about our customer base or the specific challenges we're facing?" or "Are there any external factors or industry trends that could be influencing churn?" Which PARE framework component focuses on prompting the AI to generate alternatives and augment the conversation with its own questions? Select the best answer. |Alternatives|Evaluate|Refine|Parameters

radio, Step 3: Refine Examine the various alternatives and insights the AI has provided. Are there any areas that need further clarification or elaboration? Do you see any potential biases or limitations in the AI's responses? This is where you can actively guide the AI towards refining its output. For example, you might ask the AI, "Can you provide more details about this particular solution?" or "Can you explain the reasoning behind this recommendation?" You might realize that there are certain aspects you've overlooked or questions you haven't considered. Prompt the AI to refresh your understanding by asking, "Is there anything I might have missed in this analysis?" radio, In our Design Thinking approach, which planning component looks at the specific tools you will use as you work through the four questions? |People plan|Pitch plan|Research plan|Project plan

radio, As you develop your people plan, which of the following is the most important group to consider? |Only those people who are stakeholders or experts, plus thought leaders who already support your likely solution|The entire range of people your project might have an impact on, as well as stakeholders and the core project team|Primarily those people who are current customers of your product or service, including trendsetters and media influencers|Principally people in your current network (work, school, community), especially individuals who share your perspective
answers.definition: The entire range of people your project might have an impact on, as well as stakeholders and the core project team

answers.term: radio, You are discussing your research plan with a friend. The friend asks about the role of secondary data in Design Thinking. Based on our approach, which of these is your best reply? |Secondary data creates an unnecessary conflict in the project because it will contradict our stated hypothesis and planned solution.|Secondary data is the preferred method for gathering content; it allows us to learn about people without having to interview them.|Secondary data is limited to historical, quantitative information and, therefore, never used in Design Thinking projects.|Secondary data can be useful to avoid repeating existing solutions, but the heart of the research will involve gathering primary data.
answers.definition: Secondary data can be useful to avoid repeating existing solutions, but the heart of the research will involve gathering primary data.

answers.term: radio, You have started to conduct interviews. It was all going so well - and, suddenly, you feel stuck and scared! Which of the following is a recommended technique? |Pause your work to review the steps in the Design Thinking process. Decide which steps you will omit.|Inform stakeholders that Design Thinking can be used successfully by only a few people - and, apparently, not you.|Eliminate all interviews and observation. Minimize anxiety by using only secondary research resources.|Revisit your people plan. Consider how other people in your network can help you get unstuck.
answers.definition: Revisit your people plan. Consider how other people in your network can help you get unstuck.

answers.term: radio, As you do your research, you are taking careful notes. Which of the following is also a recommended practice during research? |Consider how you will share what you are learning.|Keep your findings to yourself so no one can steal your ideas.|Create a list of potential solutions now to save time later.|Adapt the new information to support your hypothesis.
answers.definition: Consider how you will share what you are learning.

answers.term: radio, Which of the following is demonstrated in Ryan Jacoby's stories of ethnographic interviews? |What people believe they are doing and what they actually do are reliably identical.|What people believe they are doing and what they actually do may be two different things.|What people say - rather than what they do - is the only accurate source for primary research.|What the interviewer informally observes is irrelevant and must be excluded from the findings.
answers.definition: What people believe they are doing and what they actually do may be two different things.

answers.term: radio, You have been asked to conduct research on an existing product. You are allowed to interview one group of people. Applying our Design Thinking approach, which of these groups is likely to be your best source for interesting insights? |People who fall in the middle of the usage "bell curve" and can represent a majority|People who don't use the product at all and can't imagine they ever would|People who are loyal customers and who sometimes tell other people about the product|People who use the product slightly more than the average amount of time
answers.definition: People who don't use the product at all and can't imagine they ever would

answers.term: radio, In our Design Thinking approach, we recommend advance preparation before ethnographic interviews. During the actual interviews, which of the following recommendations is most likely to provide helpful insights? |Use only the questions that you wrote down before the interview - never go "off script."|Ask the identical set of questions during each interview to ensure consistency across interviews.|Limit your findings to a written survey that you provide to the person being interviewed.|Follow the energy to allow an open, active conversation and new lines of questioning in each interview.
answers.definition: Follow the energy to allow an open, active conversation and new lines of questioning in each interview.

answers.term: radio, You have been invited to provide feedback on a colleague's Design Thinking project. Which of the following is your most helpful approach? |Substantive critique of deficiencies|Expert's mind|Recommended corrections|Beginner's mind

radio, Which of the following best summarizes the advice offered by Dawan Stanford in his video? |The project will become ambiguous. Hold on through that ride. The process, when you trust it, gives you something more.|The process can feel ambiguous during your first project. After you have completed one project, you will never feel that way again.|If the project suddenly appears complex and ambiguous, rush immediately to the simplest solution. It's the best route.|When you encounter factors that affect your initial framing of the challenge, something has gone horribly wrong. End the project.
answers.definition: The project will become ambiguous. Hold on through that ride. The process, when you trust it, gives you something more.

answers.term: radio, Which of these is a fundamental requirement for finding innovation opportunities? |A lucky discovery|An extraordinary genius|A prepared mind|An accidental invention

radio, Which of these best describes a "natural law" governing the physics of growth and innovation as discussed in our course? |The overarching goal must be to eliminate variation and waste.|The only certainty is uncertainty.|Certainty and predictability are essential to success.|Priorities for any win include big budgets and predictable outcomes.

radio, Your organization wants to be more innovative! As an organization starts looking for innovative solutions, which of the following recommendations is most likely to support success? |Focus all efforts on the biggest, most obvious wins so that everyone can see them.|Survey your core customers. They are the best people to envision solutions that don't already exist.|Insist on complete, comprehensive wins ("home runs"). Anything else is not worth the time and effort.|Start small and avoid dismissing opportunities before their potential can be assessed.
answers.definition: Start small and avoid dismissing opportunities before their potential can be assessed.

answers.term: radio, Your organization wants to overcome "growth gridlock" and the physics of stability. Which of the following is a recommended method to increase opportunities for the physics of innovation? |Use data from the known past to identify where the future will be the same and plot a detailed course to that exact future.|Look for areas where the future may diverge from the past, even if this involves areas of uncertainty.|Subject all new initiatives to immediate validation through established, rigorous analytics.|Prove the future business case with today's data and expert opinions before starting any new project.
answers.definition: Look for areas where the future may diverge from the past, even if this involves areas of uncertainty.

answers.term: radio, According to our research, what are three essential factors that characterize a prepared mind? |Specialized skills, dedicated career path, functional silos|Sales expertise, customer focus, market specialist|Learning mindset, broad repertoire, customer empathy|Industry expertise, perfectionism, unwillingness to fail
answers.definition: Learning mindset, broad repertoire, customer empathy

answers.term: radio, At its best, organizational innovation is primarily about creating which of the following? |Novelty|Archival data sets|Value|Consistent progress

radio, Which of these mindsets is most likely to lead to successful innovation? |Develop a specialized, deep repertoire.|Focus on advancement, growth and accomplishment.|Avoid the possibility of negative outcomes.|Prioritize protection and safety.
answers.definition: Focus on advancement, growth and accomplishment.

answers.term: radio, You are helping your company grow! Which of the following should be "front and center" as you move forward to innovate? |Published research and opinions|Extensive risk analysis|Customer problems|Company products and services

radio, Your friend is interested in becoming more innovative at work and has asked for your help. Which piece of advice is most likely to help this new innovator? |Stick with what has worked for you in the past. It's the only way to manage anxiety.|Avoid making mistakes. Innovation is a high-stakes game and failure is not an option.|Embrace the chaos of creativity. Each of us must invent our own path to innovation.|Consider working with a structure and a process. It sounds paradoxical but it's true.
answers.definition: Consider working with a structure and a process. It sounds paradoxical but it's true.

answers.term: radio, You are excited to expand your own mind for innovation. Which of the following is the best way to accomplish this? |Commit exclusively to your current roles (work, school, community) to become an expert in one area.|Identify the safest route to success and chart your path. Avoid failure at all costs.|Look for patterns and interconnections between seemingly disparate elements. Build on them.|Work within your comfort zone so that you can focus on and deepen your existing strengths.
answers.definition: Look for patterns and interconnections between seemingly disparate elements. Build on them.

answers.term: radio, The MeYouHealth story focuses on a challenge: Engaging people in doing something about their own well-being. When Chris Cartter first encountered the challenge, what was his initial feeling? |It was an interesting concept - and too risky a challenge for Design Thinking.|It was a big question - and too big a challenge for Design Thinking.|It was an inspiring idea - and too small a challenge for Design Thinking.|It was a big question - and an area of opportunity he wanted to explore.
answers.definition: It was a big question - and an area of opportunity he wanted to explore.

answers.term: radio, Imagine that - similar to the MeYouHealth team - you are using an ethnographic approach to answer the "What Is" question. Which of the following interview strategies would you recommend to your team? |Go deep with a small number of interviews, rather than wide with a large number.|Talk primarily to people who are most likely to prove that the initial solution is good.|Schedule all interviews with industry experts to identify users' unarticulated needs quickly.|Go broad with hundreds of interviews to create one average composite of all users.
answers.definition: Go deep with a small number of interviews, rather than wide with a large number.

answers.term: radio, You want to learn even more about your interview subjects. Which of the following are examples of projective tools and approaches that you might use? |Sales forecasts based on year-to-date results|Journals, collages and pinwheels|Project plan, people plan and research plan|Customer segmentation and competitive data

radio, You are working with a team on a Design Thinking project. During the "What Is" question, you begin to see patterns and themes emerging from your interviews. Exciting! Which of the following tools would you recommend to the team, to facilitate the search for patterns and themes and to capture systematic differences? |Value chain analysis and storyboarding|Secondary research and direct observation|360 empathy and learning launches|Mind mapping and personas

radio, Your design team is ready to generate some ideas! Using your knowledge of Design Thinking, which of the following approaches would you recommend? |Ask individuals to write down ten new uses for a paper clip. Share answers. Award a prize. Assign the project challenge as homework.|Ask trigger questions. Allow individuals time for idea writing. Share results. Repeat.|Focus on the largest project goals. To save time, ignore everything but the single, best solution.|Work as a large group. Allocate most of the meeting time and idea credit to the highest-paid person in the room.
answers.definition: Ask trigger questions. Allow individuals time for idea writing. Share results. Repeat.

answers.term: radio, For Design Thinking teams, which of these is often the most difficult part of the entire design process? |Conducting research|Identifying insights|Drafting a design brief|Framing the scope
radio, Which of these is a primary goal of the Identifying Insights step? |Market a concept to customers.|Select the best solution.|Sell the solution to stakeholders.|Establish design criteria.

radio, Which of the following best describes the purpose of the gallery walk? |Encourage stakeholders to interpret our findings and share their conclusions.|Create a structured approach to converge on a key set of design insights.|Enable the team to test-drive prototypes, compare results and vote on their favorites.|Establish a creative, unstructured environment that allows visitors to critique solutions.
answers.definition: Create a structured approach to converge on a key set of design insights.

answers.term: radio, Your team has just completed a gallery walk. The team has organized the many sticky notes into clusters. What is the team's next best task? |Discard any "outliers."|Draw an insight out of each cluster.|Limit your team to one pass at the process, to focus creativity.|Highlight project facts and research observations.
answers.definition: Draw an insight out of each cluster.

answers.term: radio, Your team has asked you to define "design criteria." Which of the following is your best response? |A quick-reference checklist itemizing all of our possible solutions|A comprehensive description and prototype of our likely solution|A concise expression of the ideal end-state of our project|Step-by-step instructions detailing what to make and how to make it
answers.definition: A concise expression of the ideal end-state of our project

answers.term: radio, Which of the following best describes the Design Thinking step of brainstorming? |An opportunity to review and select best ideas from the existing choices|A disciplined, repeatable process to help create many possible alternatives|An activity to feature selected members of the team showcasing their creativity skills|An unstructured session to generate new prototypes and solutions
answers.definition: A disciplined, repeatable process to help create many possible alternatives

answers.term: radio, You are leading a Design Thinking team. The team has identified a good opportunity for Design Thinking, framed an initial project scope, and drafted a design brief. As you look ahead, which of these is the first, best time for you to conduct a brainstorming session? |At the beginning of the "What Wows" stage|At the beginning of the "What Works" stage|At the beginning of the "What If" stage|At the beginning of the "What Is" stage
answers.definition: At the beginning of the "What If" stage

answers.term: radio, To establish a successful brainstorming session, Rachel Brozenske recommends considering three aspects. What are they? |Customers, stakeholders, team members|Environment, session, action|Creative people, non-creative people, notetakers|Risk, reward, return on investment

radio, Which of the following is the best guidance for conducting an effective Design Thinking brainstorming session? |Some people's ideas are more important than others.|It's better to judge each idea immediately before moving on to the next.|There is no such thing as a bad idea.|There's no risk in writing down a bad idea.
answers.definition: There's no risk in writing down a bad idea.

answers.term: radio, During the brainstorming session, Rachel Brozenske recommends setting a tone that enables participants to focus on "ideas" rather than "qualities." Your team asks you to explain the difference. Which of the following is your best response? |An idea is valuable, but a quality is useless.|An idea is easier to generate than a quality.|An idea is less concrete than a quality and, therefore, more flexible.|An idea makes a quality actionable.
answers.definition: An idea makes a quality actionable.

answers.term: radio, You are facilitating a brainstorming session. Which of the following tools are your best choice to help participants generate ideas? |Secondary research and prototypes|Trigger questions and analogies|Value chain analyses and storyboards|Direct observation and journey mapping

radio, You have just completed a brainstorming session. During the session, your wonderful team generated - literally - hundreds of ideas! What is your next, best step? |Focus on creating prototypes based on the best ideas from the session.|Schedule a formal break between brainstorming and concept development to let new ideas take shape.|Agree on logistics and assign roles for the first learning launch.|Move quickly from brainstorming into concept development.
answers.definition: Move quickly from brainstorming into concept development.

answers.term: radio, A team member has asked you to explain the difference between brainstorming and concept development. Which of these is your best explanation? |Concept development sets aside the informal "warm up" ideas generated in brainstorming and focuses on the formal design brief.|Concept development selects the best ideas from brainstorming and distills them into a single, recommended solution.|Concept development takes individual ideas generated during brainstorming and combines them into powerful bundles for evaluating against our criteria.|Concept development invites a diverse group of people from outside the core team to develop potential solutions based on brainstorming results.
answers.definition: Concept development takes individual ideas generated during brainstorming and combines them into powerful bundles for evaluating against our criteria.

answers.term: radio, You want to assist your team by providing a Design Thinking tool during concept development. Which of these is your best choice? |Storyboard|360 empathy tool|Chili table|Value chain analysis
radio, After a brainstorming session, we want to take action by doing two things. What are they? |Research and beta test|Review and discard|Organize and combine|Prototype and launch

radio, A friend asks you to explain the purpose of the Design Thinking napkin pitch. Which of the following is your best reply? |An annotated graph outlining detailed, annual revenue forecasts for our solution|A two-minute, verbal overview of our entire project (similar to the "elevator pitch" in sales)|A simple, consistent format for summarizing and communicating our concepts|A map showing the step-by-step journey from our solution to the marketplace
answers.definition: A simple, consistent format for summarizing and communicating our concepts

answers.term: radio, Which of the following is a benefit of using napkin pitches in Design Thinking? |Explore multiple options and let other people validate them.|Showcase the unique benefits of the single, best solution.|Provide stakeholders with a complete, detailed look into the project process and solution.|Support a variety of different template formats, one per pitch.
answers.definition: Explore multiple options and let other people validate them.

answers.term: radio, The Design Thinking "wow zone" is at the intersection of three "wow" measurements. What are they? |Customer, execution, business-model|Past sales, current revenue, future projections|Product, marketplace, competition|Quality, schedule, budget

radio, In our case study of IBM trade shows, the George P. Johnson (GPJ) design team began by stepping away from existing models of trade shows. Which of the following Design Thinking techniques does the team's action demonstrate? |Developing concepts|Prototyping|Reframing|Journey mapping

radio, Your team is ready to tackle step 11: Surface key assumptions. A team member asks you why this step is important. Which of the following is your best reply? |This step gives us the opportunity to market-test our new solution.|This step enables us to gather data about why our assumptions may or may not be true.|This step enables us to create a journey map for the intended customer.|This step enables us to prove that all our original assumptions are correct.
answers.definition: This step enables us to gather data about why our assumptions may or may not be true.

answers.term: radio, Your team is ready to begin testing key assumptions. Which of the following techniques is the fastest, lowest-cost, lowest-risk way to test an assumption when you already have the necessary data? |Thought experiment|Field experiment|High-fidelity prototype experiment|Learning launch experiment

radio, You have worked with your team to brainstorm ideas, develop concepts, create napkin pitches and surface key assumptions. Great work! You are ready to introduce assumption testing. What is the purpose of assumption testing? |Meet with stakeholders to tell them that our solution is what customers really want.|Position the solution prominently in our organization's product/service portfolio.|Identify the "make-or-break" (absolute success or failure) elements of our concepts.|Launch new concepts in the marketplace to see if they sell.
answers.definition: Identify the "make-or-break" (absolute success or failure) elements of our concepts.

answers.term: radio, Your design team is still in the early stages of innovation - and they are ready to test assumptions. You have explained that assumption testing includes four key tests. Of the four key tests, which two are generally the most important to test first? |Market campaigns and tracking|Value and execution|Sales strategies and positioning|Scale and sustainability

radio, Which of the following is a best practice for conducting thought experiments? |Finalize the solution before beginning.|Take a hypothesis-driven approach.|Select the solution using an either-or approach.|Focus attention on one answer.

radio, Your team wants to test an assumption, but past data sources do not provide sufficient help. Which of the following is the best, lowest-risk way to test assumptions when you need more than the existing, published data? |Thought experiment|Field experiment|Secondary research|Design brief

radio, You want to test your value-creation assumptions. Which of the following is a recommended technique to help users "pre-experience" your concept? |Prototype|Online survey|Focus group|Design criteria

radio, Your team is getting ready to create early prototypes. They ask you to explain a "good prototype." Which of the following is your best guidance? |It always shows the end-to-end experience in its entirety.|It always shows the solution with choices already made for the user.|It always tells a story that invites other people into the experience with you.|It always presents a three-dimensional, polished version of the final product.
answers.definition: It always tells a story that invites other people into the experience with you.

answers.term: radio, Your team has decided to take Dave Bishop's recommendation and use a "continuum of prototyping." Which of the following is a key advantage of this approach? |The continuum enables us to focus exclusively on building actual, polished products.|The continuum supports an immediate, successful entry of fully functional products into the market.|The continuum enables us to justify our greatest expenditures at the beginning of the continuum.|The continuum offers a high return on investment throughout the prototyping process.
answers.definition: The continuum offers a high return on investment throughout the prototyping process.

answers.term: radio, You have been asked to prototype a user interface consisting of 50-100 screens. You are testing for usability. Which of the following is your best choice? |Research the interface so that you can defend all screens to a user. When a user hesitates or asks a question, state the rationale.|Learn more about the users so that you can focus the prototype on the screens the user is most likely to care about.|Solve the problem by cleaning up the interface so that the screens are more attractive to the user.|Show all the screens exactly as originally provided, in order to prototype the complete experience for the user.
answers.definition: Learn more about the users so that you can focus the prototype on the screens the user is most likely to care about.

answers.term: radio, You are conducting an early usability test for a new medical kiosk. Your goals are to make the kiosk easier to use and more inviting. Which of the following is a best practice for your first prototype? |The interaction can be created with simple materials, such as paper and pen.|The final technology should be in place to demonstrate the actual patient experience.|The prototype will place doctors and patients in a live setting, conducting the medical test.|The kiosk must be fully built and functional to provide the physical experience.
answers.definition: The interaction can be created with simple materials, such as paper and pen.

answers.term: radio, You are sharing your prototype with a potential customer. The person is providing feedback! What is your best response? |Listen to the feedback. Ask clarifying questions.|Point out the customer's best options. Explain why they are correct.|Apologize for the rough, unfinished quality of the prototype. State that you will wait to collect feedback until you can provide a more polished version.|Explain that the prototype is near final. State that changes are no longer possible.
answers.definition: Listen to the feedback. Ask clarifying questions.

answers.term: radio, You are conducting an early prototyping session with a stakeholder. The stakeholder says, "Well, I see this part and this part - but how would the next thing happen?" Which of the following is your strongest reply? |Here's what should happen next.|What makes sense to you?|I'm delighted to explain.|That's not important.

radio, You are preparing to conduct a co-creation session with a stakeholder. Your shared goal is to improve the customer experience. Which is your best choice to bring with you to the meeting? |Twenty-five slides|Fifty-page report|The finished product|One poster

radio, You want to learn more about which potential features of your solution might appeal to a specific group of users. You plan to meet with one target user. Which of the following is a recommended co-creation technique? |5Bs supply chain map|Napkin pitch|Design brief|Card sort

radio, Your team wants to know what potential users are feeling and to obtain quick feedback on your new concept. Which of these is your best method? |Co-creation|Focus group|Online survey|Secondary research

radio, A friend asks you to explain the goal of a Design Thinking learning launch. Which of the following is your best response? |Collect user feedback on surveys.|Prove a stated set of outcomes.|Set aside data about potential weaknesses.|Test remaining critical assumptions.

radio, You and your design team have created prototypes, run co-creation sessions with stakeholders, and incorporated feedback into your prototype. Now you want to test your concept with a wider audience. You are ready to design a learning launch. Which of the following is essential to a successful learning launch? |Make the experience feel genuine.|Keep the prototype unfinished to invite co-creation.|Test multiple options to provide choices.|Limit the team to strong supporters of innovation.

radio, Your team is preparing for its first learning launch. Which of the following is a desired outcome of a first learning launch? |All assumptions tested and proven|A set of metrics that will allow us to go back and improve the solution we've created|An experience with no dissent, conflict, or surprises|A general idea of our primary audience
answers.definition: A set of metrics that will allow us to go back and improve the solution we've created

answers.term: radio, In Tim Ogilvie's explanation of in-market experiments, he talks about shifting our focus to key assumptions. Which of the following is the most accurate statement throughout that shift? |User needs are set aside to focus on execution.|User needs are set aside to focus on cost.|User needs are still here.|User needs are set aside in favor of scalability.

radio, Tim Ogilvie discusses similarities between conducting in-market experimentation and launching a start-up business. During in-market experimentation, which of the following is the most important assumption to test? |Our stakeholders can protect it from budget cuts.|Our customers want it.|Our suppliers can build it.|Our manufacturers can scale it.

radio, Which of the following is the most effective use of the thought experiments layer (row) in a learning plan timeline? |Revisit the thought experiments layer throughout the timeline.|Use the thought experiments layer once, at the beginning of the timeline.|Eliminate the thought experiments layer whenever possible, to manage expenses.|Focus resources on the thought experiments layer as the primary method of producing the live experience.
answers.definition: Revisit the thought experiments layer throughout the timeline.

answers.term: radio, Your team wants to conduct a 4D (four-dimensional), live, in-market experiment. Which of the following is your best choice for the prototype? |Card sort|Persona|Poster|Lemonade stand

radio, Your team is creating the prototype for a 4D (four-dimensional), live, in-market experiment. Which of the following is a recommended characteristic of the prototype? |Completely built and ready to display in stores so that users will see it the next day|Completely built on a scalable platform so that the actual product can be sold to users during the test|Polished and finished to encourage users to believe it is the real thing (even though parts of it are still fake)|Rough and unfinished to encourage users to change things and provide input throughout the experiment
answers.definition: Polished and finished to encourage users to believe it is the real thing (even though parts of it are still fake)

answers.term: radio, Tim Ogilvie discusses validity-oriented thinking, based on concepts introduced by Roger Martin. Which of the following is a characteristic of validity thinking? |Possibility oriented|Proof oriented|Predictability oriented|Repeatability oriented

radio, You and your design team have been working through the Design Thinking process, developing what may be an innovative product! The team is ready to perform an in-market experiment. A team member asks you for guidance about the relationship between the in-market experiment and metrics. Which of the following is your best guidance? |We must achieve all the metric targets, or we will need to consider the experiment a failure.|We may fail on hitting the metric targets, but we must not fail on the learning.|We will establish the metrics after the experiment so that we can match them to the responses.|We should set aside the metrics for this experiment so that we can focus on the user.
answers.definition: We may fail on hitting the metric targets, but we must not fail on the learning.

answers.term: radio, You and your colleagues are actively seeking ways to improve the new-hire experience at your organization. Your team has been working through the steps of the Design Thinking process. Earlier today, you conducted an initial learning launch. Overall, the results of the learning launch looked promising! What is your next, best step? |Invest resources up front to get ahead of new learning.|Congratulate the team and deliver the finished project.|Set aside Design Thinking and return to traditional analysis.|Iterate based on the results and revisit steps as needed.
answers.definition: Iterate based on the results and revisit steps as needed.

answers.term: radio, When considering the overall risk/investment relationship in a Design Thinking project, which of the following would you test for first? |Need|Marketplace|Scale|Concept

radio, Joshua Marcuse introduced the importance/difficulty matrix as a method for prioritizing ideas and determining which ideas to focus on. Which of the following is a suggested best practice when using the matrix? |Build a portfolio of ideas. Ask yourself, "What are things I could do...?"|Force-rank both the difficulty and the importance.|Treat each idea as a separate, standalone concept.|Have at least one idea in each of the four quadrants.
answers.definition: Build a portfolio of ideas. Ask yourself, "What are things I could do...?"

answers.term: radio, Jeanne Liedtka used a "waterline" graphic to discuss the potential impact of Design Thinking on people. Which of the following is true about the relationship between Design Thinking processes and people's behaviors? |Behaviors related to Design Thinking can be observed, monitored, encouraged, and perhaps even measured.|Behaviors above the waterline are the least measurable in a Design Thinking environment.|Design Thinking helps users set aside disconfirming data and adjust data to the behaviors that confirm their view.|Design Thinking processes can create new solutions, but the process has no effect on mindsets or behaviors.
answers.definition: Behaviors related to Design Thinking can be observed, monitored, encouraged, and perhaps even measured.

answers.term: radio, Which of the following is a gift of Design Thinking? |Ability to stay in the question|Ability to jump to a solution mindset|Ability to ignore disconfirming data|Ability to pilot concepts immediately
answers.definition: Ability to stay in the question

answers.term: radio, Your volunteer group will meet next week to collaborate on an idea for a fundraising event. You realize that participants may have a broad range of perspectives and goals. You have been asked to facilitate the meeting. You plan to use a Design Thinking approach. Which of the following is an appropriate goal for your meeting? |Finding common ground|Optimizing|Satisficing|Dismissing dissenting views

radio, In Design Thinking, which of the following contributes most strongly to our success in moving from "Ideas to Action"? |Committing to "either-or" (one or the other) thinking|Using data from experiments|Scheduling formal team debates|Creating a solution based on compromises

radio, Design Thinking can help us to curate, similar to the role of a museum curator. Which of the following best describes this opportunity? |Create an open, unstructured, creative space for stakeholders.|Display all the data so that each person can decide what is important and what isn't.|Drill down to the essence of an issue and see what really matters.|Provide each idea as a separate, independent element for review.
answers.definition: Drill down to the essence of an issue and see what really matters.

answers.term: radio, Which of the following is a strategic contribution of Design Thinking to teams and organizations? |Set aside stakeholder expectations.|Increase the visibility of and budget for new projects.|Disregard disconfirming data.|Increase the speed of learning.

radio, Which of the following is a strategic contribution of Design Thinking? |Finish the solution before sharing it with others.|Enable individuals to single-handedly create wins.|Create the perfect plan before taking any action.|Leave space in the emergence of the solution.
answers.definition: Leave space in the emergence of the solution.

answers.term: radio, Your team plans to use Design Thinking to tackle a complicated business problem. The team is working to define the problem challenge. Which of the following best expresses the relationship between a complex problem challenge and stakeholder mapping? |Stakeholder mapping is most helpful after the problem is solved, and the team is ready to present the solution to decision makers.|Stakeholder mapping is typically used to identify potential competitors and has no direct relationship to the problem definition.|Stakeholder mapping is a way to identify relevant people and reduce the risk of our solutions.|Stakeholder mapping is only appropriate after stakeholders agree on the problem definition.
answers.definition: Stakeholder mapping is a way to identify relevant people and reduce the risk of our solutions.

answers.term: radio, Your manager sees the project team working on a stakeholder map. The manager wants to know if this is a reasonable use of their time. Which of the following best describes the purpose of stakeholder mapping? |Choose the best ideas from brainstorming and assemble them into a portfolio of solutions.|Draft a list of the people who will state that our project assumptions are correct.|Identify people and groups relevant to the opportunity and whose attitudes or behaviors can affect the success of our solution.|Create a simple, consistent format for summarizing and communicating our concepts.
answers.definition: Identify people and groups relevant to the opportunity and whose attitudes or behaviors can affect the success of our solution.

answers.term: radio, You are introducing a colleague to the Design Thinking tool: stakeholder mapping. Which of the following is a benefit of stakeholder mapping? |Eliminate all risk related to our new solutions.|Agree on the best solution before beginning the project.|Remove the potential for dissent during the project.|Focus on creating value for others.
answers.definition: Focus on creating value for others.

answers.term: radio, Your team is eager to learn more about stakeholder mapping. A team member asks you how and when to use this tool during the Design Thinking process. Which of the following is your best reply? |Conduct the first stakeholder mapping session immediately before starting live, in-market experiments. Use the same map during all experiments for consistency.|Create a stakeholder map once before starting the Design Thinking project. Use it for a one-time analysis. Then, archive it as a historical record for the project files.|Wait to use the stakeholder map tool until the end of the project when the team has clearer insights. Tailor the map to show data that confirms the team's new solution.|Create a stakeholder map early in the Design Thinking process. Continue to revisit and refine the map throughout the process.
answers.definition: Create a stakeholder map early in the Design Thinking process. Continue to revisit and refine the map throughout the process.

answers.term: radio, Your team is preparing to work on a Design Thinking stakeholder map. They are not quite sure which people and groups should be included on the map. They ask your advice. Which of the following is a best practice? |Wait until the learning launch and then create a list of potential customers.|Create one persona, based on a composite of everyone interested in the project's outcomes.|When in doubt, choose on the side of creating a broader list.|Aim for a narrow, focused list of no more than five people. Set aside all others.
answers.definition: When in doubt, choose on the side of creating a broader list.

answers.term: radio, Your team members have discovered that stakeholder mapping is helpful in their current Design Thinking challenge. They want to know if it can be used in other situations, too. Which of the following best describes the types of organization settings in which stakeholder mapping can be useful? |First-time, innovative projects only|Larger, strategic-level projects only|Multiple levels, from organization-level to more fine-grained projects|Smaller, tactical-level projects only
answers.definition: Multiple levels, from organization-level to more fine-grained projects

answers.term: radio, Your team has generated an initial list of stakeholders. Using the Design Thinking approach, which of the following is your next best step? |Understand the relationship between stakeholders and the issue.|Determine which of our existing solutions the stakeholders want.|Create a prototype and pitch it to stakeholders.|Identify and focus efforts on stakeholders who support our hypothesis.
answers.definition: Understand the relationship between stakeholders and the issue.

answers.term: radio, Your team is conducting a stakeholder mapping session. A team member asks if there is any relationship between empathy and stakeholder mapping. Which of the following best describes the relationship between empathy, stakeholder mapping, and the success of your eventual solution? |Empathy is a nice-to-have in stakeholder mapping, but it is not necessary until we have moved from idea generation to actual in-market testing.|Empathy helps us identify the behavioral and attitudinal considerations for each stakeholder that are necessary for our solution to be effective.|Empathy and stakeholder mapping are two separate, unrelated topics. Stakeholder mapping focuses exclusively on job descriptions and responsibilities.|Empathy is not relevant to stakeholder mapping, but it may be helpful during ethnographic research (interviews and observation) and journey mapping.
answers.definition: Empathy helps us identify the behavioral and attitudinal considerations for each stakeholder that are necessary for our solution to be effective.

answers.term: radio, Your team is taking a coffee break - and discussing stakeholders. They wonder what is driving stakeholder behavior. Which of the following is a best practice when considering stakeholders' motivations? |Imagine all motivations in a negative light to help anticipate and overcome obstacles.|Focus only on those motivations that will support your solution.|Do not attempt to ascribe any motivations.|Frame motivations in a positive light.
answers.definition: Frame motivations in a positive light.

answers.term: radio, You have identified and met with a variety of potential stakeholders for your current Design Thinking challenge. One thing is clear from your meetings: The stakeholders can't even agree on the definition of the problem! How could you use stakeholder mapping to help you move forward? |Create an initial stakeholder map to identify each of the individuals and groups involved, as a first step towards collaborative dialogue.|Develop a formal stakeholder map. Use it to prove to the important stakeholders why some stakeholders are correct and others are wrong.|Build a stakeholder map. Structure it to feature a solution that will prove your assumptions and simplify the problem-solving process.|Create a stakeholder map. Use it to define a comfortable middle ground that is sufficiently general to minimize changes and differences.
answers.definition: Create an initial stakeholder map to identify each of the individuals and groups involved, as a first step towards collaborative dialogue.

answers.term: radio, Which of the following best describes the purpose of the Design Thinking tool: job to be done (JTBD)? |Uncover and document the desired outcome of the user.|Synthesize and group ideas during concept development.|Create a list of the specific tools the team will need in the Design Thinking process.|Test abstract ideas by creating the "pre-experience" of a new future.
answers.definition: Uncover and document the desired outcome of the user.

answers.term: radio, You have explained to the team that the job to be done tool is a critical piece of your innovation project. A team member asks why. Which of these is your best response? |It emphasizes the products and services that users have said they want, based on surveys and focus groups.|It helps focus our work on what the user is trying to accomplish, and it may reframe the project.|It determines the set of industries and market sectors that are most likely to want our solution.|It provides a list of customer market segments so that we can position products and services within the segments.
answers.definition: It helps focus our work on what the user is trying to accomplish, and it may reframe the project.

answers.term: radio, The job to be done tool has two components. One component is "emotional." What is the other component? |Corporate|Financial|Functional|Strategic

radio, Which of the following best describes the emotional component of the Design Thinking tool: job to be done? |It is essential to our solution's success but difficult for users to articulate.|It is the existing, generally accepted version of the primary goal of the product or service.|It is the readily available, published information on the product package or website.|It is the series of stated actions that must be completed by any user of the product or service.
answers.definition: It is essential to our solution's success but difficult for users to articulate.

answers.term: radio, You and a colleague are getting ready to conduct an ethnographic interview. You recommend creating an ethnographic interview guide (sometimes called a discussion guide). Your colleague asks you to describe the purpose of a guide. Which of the following is your best response? |A graphic representation of the overlapping area where customer, execution and business-model intersect|A list that describes the attributes of an ideal solution|A plan for the interview, including topics and fail-safe|A consistent format for summarizing and communicating our ideas
answers.definition: A plan for the interview, including topics and fail-safe

answers.term: radio, You and your colleague are planning to conduct an ethnographic interview with a potential user. You have chosen your interview roles. Your colleague will be notetaker. You will be interviewer. As interviewer, which of the following is your best approach during the main questions portion of the interview? |A brief summary statement proving why your problem definition is correct and requesting a supporting quote|Open-ended questions and perhaps an empathy-building activity|Closed-ended questions and verified statistics to establish clear topic boundaries|A series of low-priority questions first to get them out of the way, followed by a gradual transition to higher-priority questions
answers.definition: Open-ended questions and perhaps an empathy-building activity

answers.term: radio, As shown in our videos, the Kingwood design team applied Design Thinking throughout their work. Which of the following best describes their approach to initial research? |Devote time to deep discovery and to the development of empathy.|Stay strictly within the traditional rules of existing research tools.|Talk directly with end users to find out the best answers immediately.|Limit the involvement of stakeholders until the final presentation.
answers.definition: Devote time to deep discovery and to the development of empathy.

answers.term: radio, As shown in our Kingwood story, an important element of Design Thinking is our ability to define the problem. Which of the following does our Kingwood story best illustrate? |Successful design begins with the nature of the questions that we ask.|For an ideal solution, we should set our questions and challenges with no boundaries.|A traditional industry focus is the safest and most reliable approach.|The best problem definition focuses on removing pain points and preventing bad events.
answers.definition: Successful design begins with the nature of the questions that we ask.

answers.term: radio, Your design team has invited stakeholders to a workshop. Your workshop goal: Imagine an ideal, shared garden space. To prepare, your team set up a patch of (fake) grass. They created cards and stickers showing possible garden elements and activities. (They also left a few blank cards and stickers for participants' ideas.) During the workshop, you will ask participants to place the cards and stickers in areas of preference on the grass. You hope to get an idea of what could be popular in the final garden space. Which Design Thinking technique does this best describe? |Design brief|Secondary research|Value chain analysis|Co-creation

radio, You and your team want to use Design Thinking to improve people's lives through innovative solutions. You already know that tackling these challenges will take you into new, uncharted terrain. Which of the following is a typical characteristic of most of the people you wish to serve? |Most people will have limits on their ability to correctly articulate their needs.|Our stakeholders are experts who can clearly articulate the needs of all users, based on past data.|Most people can clearly articulate their own needs if we ask them.|If we put ourselves in the minds of the people we want to serve, we can easily articulate their needs.
answers.definition: Most people will have limits on their ability to correctly articulate their needs.

answers.term: radio, You and your team are using Design Thinking to reinvent the product delivery experience for customers. Today you will introduce the team to a powerful Design Thinking tool: the journey map. Which of the following best describes the purpose of a customer journey map? |Understand the current reality of the customer.|Create a matrix showing the full range of customer segments.|Apply traditional analytical methods to areas of high uncertainty.|Distill customer-preference survey results into an easy-to-understand summary.
answers.definition: Understand the current reality of the customer.

answers.term: radio, You are explaining the Design Thinking process to your family. They are particularly intrigued by the journey map tool. They want to know how a map could possibly help you create a new solution. Why are journey maps important to the Design Thinking process? |Build empathy for our users and identify unmet needs.|Fit the customer into our organization's top priorities and processes.|Generate simple, immediate solutions.|Identify and focus on stated needs.
answers.definition: Build empathy for our users and identify unmet needs.

answers.term: radio, You and your team are getting ready to create a customer journey map. It is the team's first experience with creating a map! A team member asks you the difference between a Design Thinking journey map and a traditional business process map (a flow diagram with boxes and connectors). Which of the following is your best response? |A customer journey map is created to demonstrate that our solution is correct.|A customer journey map includes the parts of the customer's journey that we can't see.|A customer journey map presents only functional tasks, without any emotional components.|A customer journey map focuses primarily on the customer's words rather than on the customer's actions.
answers.definition: A customer journey map includes the parts of the customer's journey that we can't see.

answers.term: radio, You are showing your Design Thinking journey map to a friend. Which of the following best describes a key characteristic of the journey's "moments of truth"? |Emotional|Irrelevant|Statistical|Obvious

radio, Your team has developed their first Design Thinking journey map. The map traces the journey of a potential new customer. You are ready to work with the team to identify key takeaways (learnings) from the map. Which of the following is typically a takeaway of journey mapping? |Document that outlines the people you may need to interview or observe|Initial prototype of a solution concept|Blueprint for what's happening with the customer|Step-by-step plan for a learning launch
answers.definition: Blueprint for what's happening with the customer

answers.term: radio, Your team wants to create a Design Thinking journey map of a potential customer. The team will show the map to organizational executives and managers. Which of these is a recommended journey map format? |A comprehensive text report explaining how customers respond to marketing campaigns|A set of statistical tables showing customer buying patterns and product preferences|A big visual showing the journey in time, from beginning to end (left to right)|A one-page 2x2 matrix, capturing the characteristics of various users (customers, stakeholders)
answers.definition: A big visual showing the journey in time, from beginning to end (left to right)

answers.term: radio, You have identified your problem challenge: improve the buyer's experience during an online purchase from your store. You decide to create a customer journey map. Which of these is your best, first task? |Determine the high and low points in the journey.|Select the people whose experience you want to understand.|Prove your hypothesis before creating the map, to maximize efficiency.|Identify patterns and themes across people's experiences.
answers.definition: Select the people whose experience you want to understand.

answers.term: radio, Your team plans to conduct ethnographic interviews with students who are deciding next steps in their education. The team will then use the interview findings to create journey maps. Knowing this, which of the following is a best practice during the actual interviews? |Ask close-ended questions to prove the team's hypothesis.|Limit questions to the predefined problem challenge.|Avoid questions. Aim to keep the conversation completely unstructured.|Ask questions about topics that are larger than the journey itself.
answers.definition: Ask questions about topics that are larger than the journey itself.

answers.term: radio, Your team is in the "What Is" stage of the Design Thinking process. They interviewed more than a dozen potential users. Then they created an initial journey map for each user. The team enthusiastically asks you what you recommend next. Which of the following is a next, best step? |Move immediately to concept development.|Build a prototype.|Look for themes.|Set up a learning launch.

radio, Your team is creating a customer journey map. As they map the steps, you encourage them also to include information about the various people, objects, and places that are part of the customer's journey. Which of the following is the best reason for this recommendation? |Create a simple, consistent format for summarizing and communicating solution concepts.|Begin to build the initial framework of what the customer's experience looks like.|Test the remaining set of critical assumptions.|Ensure that the organization can scale the solution.
answers.definition: Begin to build the initial framework of what the customer's experience looks like.

answers.term: radio, A team member asks you to describe Design Thinking personas. Which of the following is your best response? |Team members who agree to take the independent lead on concept development|Stakeholders who champion our solution within the organization|Fictional characters based on data from our ethnographic research|Specific colleagues, friends and family who are willing to participate in the testing process
answers.definition: Fictional characters based on data from our ethnographic research

answers.term: radio, Your team has been examining their ethnographic research data. Themes and patterns are beginning to emerge! The happy team wants to know what to do next. You suggest that they use the persona tool. Why? |Identify the most frequently stated need and focus on it.|Classify results into demographic segments.|Uncover unarticulated needs.|Estimate the market size as represented by each interviewee.

radio, You are talking with a friend about your Design Thinking challenge. You explain that your team is developing personas. The friend says that it sounds like fun but wonders if it is also useful. Which of the following is your best answer to explain the power of personas? |Remove any disconfirming data from our interviews to strengthen our business case.|Enhance our ability to build empathy with the people we wish to serve.|Separate us from the emotions of our interviewees, so that we can focus on solutions.|Identify the one, actual interviewee who best represents our customer market.
answers.definition: Enhance our ability to build empathy with the people we wish to serve.

answers.term: radio, Your team is ready to develop personas. They want to know how to begin. Which of the following is a recommended first step? |Summarize and communicate multiple new concepts consistently and completely, to help make choices.|Identify a number of dimensions that seem to reveal important differences across interviewees.|Clarify the scope, intent, questions, and stakeholders for the innovation journey.|Create a "lemonade stand" prototype as a live, in-market experiment.
answers.definition: Identify a number of dimensions that seem to reveal important differences across interviewees.

answers.term: radio, Your team has spent time with the ethnographic research results, identifying themes and similarities. They have also identified several useful differences. Exciting! What is the team's next best step? |Proceed to concept development.|Schedule a learning launch.|Test the defensibility of your solution.|Play with various combinations of the differences.
answers.definition: Play with various combinations of the differences.

answers.term: radio, Your team is ready to begin identifying the dimensions that will help them develop personas. You explain that the team can work with various formats - and that you recommend the "two by two" matrix (2x2 chart drawn with two axes to create four quadrants). Why? |It specifies our assumptions about value, execution, scale, and sustainability.|It gives the team a straightforward method and a manageable number to work with.|It clarifies the scope of our process, intent, target audience, and stakeholders.|It provides a proven method to help us test potential solutions on a small scale.
answers.definition: It gives the team a straightforward method and a manageable number to work with.

answers.term: radio, Your team has created many two-by-two persona matrices (2x2 matrixes). Team members have placed sticky notes in quadrants of the various matrices. The sticky notes represent each of the people they've interviewed. The notes are placed in whatever quadrants seem appropriate. Now the team feels ready to choose one or more persona matrices to move forward with. Which of the following is your best-practice recommendation for selection? |Select the matrices that have most of the sticky notes in one quadrant.|Select the matrices that have sticky notes in at least three of the four quadrants.|Select the matrices that have most of the sticky notes in two quadrants.|Select the matrices that have no sticky notes.
answers.definition: Select the matrices that have sticky notes in at least three of the four quadrants.

answers.term: radio, You are telling your neighbor about the use of personas in Design Thinking. Which of the following is a goal of generating personas? |Size the potential market.|Test our preferred solutions.|Prove our initial hypothesis.|Create more innovative ideas.

radio, You and your team have identified the personas that you wish to explore. You suggest that the team work together to map the journey of each persona. Which of the following is the most compelling reason to perform this task? |Identify the low points in each persona's journey.|Identify the neutral points in each persona's journey.|Identify the high points in each persona's journey.|Identify the merchandising potential in each persona's journey.
answers.definition: Identify the low points in each persona's journey.

answers.term: radio, Your team has decided to use the "two by two" (2x2) format to create persona matrices. Which of the following best describes the role (purpose) of the two axes in a 2x2 persona matrix? |Show which quadrants are correct and which are wrong.|Design a compromise solution for the entire demographic group.|Discern between observed behavioral habits.|Judge between good and bad user characteristics.

radio, Your team is implementing design thinking for the first time. What intrateam dynamic would you NOT expect to result from the DT process? |Improved trust among team members|Enhanced engagement of employees during stakeholder conversations|Increased employee empowerment resulting from clearly defined responsibilities assigned to each team member|A sense of shared purpose and greater commitment to collaboration
answers.definition: Increased employee empowerment resulting from clearly defined responsibilities assigned to each team member

answers.term: radio, A member of your team recently went through a crisis in their personal life. You notice they are dismissive of almost every idea your team suggests, despite having supported several of them just a week before. This is an example of which type of bias? |Egocentric Empathy Gap|Hot/Cold Gap|Category 2 Bias|Availability Bias

radio, John has joined a team that is developing a branding solution for a client, and he wants to use this opportunity to become a better designer and innovator. Which of the following should be John's chief focus during the design thinking process? |Not quite. Delivering choices that create better value in the moment for his client|Immersing himself in the users' lives|Not quite. Improving long-term choices by making both individuals and organizations more adaptable in a changing world|Not quite. Reducing the risk and cost of innovation efforts
answers.definition: Immersing himself in the users' lives

answers.term: radio, Danny wants to use DT to gain a better understanding of his stakeholders. His team is new to the DT process. What should he do to help make his team more comfortable with DT's new way of thinking? |DT is a creative process, so he should give them as much flexibility implementing the principles as possible and avoid giving them specific instruction|Acquire market analysis so his team can familiarize itself with quantitative data about the stakeholders upfront|Get his team excited by having them brainstorm potential solutions right from the beginning|Help his team feel safe by outlining a structured and facilitated creative process for them to follow
answers.definition: Help his team feel safe by outlining a structured and facilitated creative process for them to follow

answers.term: radio, Maria is a project manager working on a branding campaign for an electronics company, and she wants to improve her design thinking process. She feels that in the past she has focused too much on her own view of what works, and wants to become more open to the ideas and concerns of both her coworkers and her target audience. To achieve this growth, which of the following mindset shifts would she want to avoid undertaking? |Being detached and distant to being more curious and personally engaged|Being certain about the accuracy of her own perspective to being aware of her own personal biases|Going from egocentric to empathetic|Going from empathetic to egocentric

radio, Which of the following is the best example of the experience of immersion? |A project manager is trying to design a more effective product delivery system. She reviews data on delivery times and late delivery alerts.|The owner of a food truck notices that the line is much longer on Tuesdays than it is any other day of the week. He then works to secure additional volunteers to prepare and serve food on Tuesday, thus reducing the wait time of his patrons.|A public health official is looking to design a better outreach program for her city. She tours local hospitals, holds open discussions with concerned citizens, and gains a new perspective and appreciation for the struggles of the community.|The manager of a restaurant is trying to redesign her menu offerings. She tracks the orders made by her patrons to determine which foods are most popular. She then conducts surveys to determine if patron sentiment matches her quantitative data.
answers.definition: A public health official is looking to design a better outreach program for her city. She tours local hospitals, holds open discussions with concerned citizens, and gains a new perspective and appreciation for the struggles of the community.

answers.term: radio, Which of the following is the best example of the experience of immersion? |A project manager is trying to design a more effective product delivery system. She reviews data on delivery times and late delivery alerts.|The owner of a food truck notices that the line is much longer on Tuesdays than it is any other day of the week. He then works to secure additional volunteers to prepare and serve food on Tuesday, thus reducing the wait time of his patrons.|A public health official is looking to design a better outreach program for her city. She tours local hospitals, holds open discussions with concerned citizens, and gains a new perspective and appreciation for the struggles of the community.|The manager of a restaurant is trying to redesign her menu offerings. She tracks the orders made by her patrons to determine which foods are most popular. She then conducts surveys to determine if patron sentiment matches her quantitative data.
answers.definition: A mayor looking to design programs to better meet the needs of his city's homeless population. He visits soup kitchens for food, tours shelter facilities, and gains a new perspective and appreciation for the struggles of the homeless population.

answers.term: radio, Which of the following is true when it comes to experiencing immersion? |Fear can increase our willingness to engage with others|Our biases can blind us|Cultivating curiosity is not important|It definitely does not involve the mirror nuerons in our brain

radio, Jessica is the leader of a project design team. As she conducts her research and investigation, she knows she needs to be wary of several natural human tendencies to achieve true immersion. Which of the following would NOT be an example of these tendencies? |Once she has identified several hypotheses, Jessica gathers data to prove they are worth pursuing.|As she conducts an interview, Jessica finds herself automatically judging her subjects' beliefs when they do not match up with her own.|Jessica is unsure where her research will ultimately take her but is curious about the end-user perspective on her product. She confidently walks up to strangers and talks to them about their experience with her product.|During ethnographic research, Jessica uncovers new information, realizes its importance, creates a hypothesis, and redirects the interview to target her new hypothesis.
answers.definition: Jessica is unsure where her research will ultimately take her but is curious about the end-user perspective on her product. She confidently walks up to strangers and talks to them about their experience with her product.

answers.term: radio, Which of the following should Jill be sure to do during the design thinking process? |Look for extreme users to help figure out what future is already happening|Use her subject matter expertise to help non-experts better understand her ideas|Rely on quantitative data to prove her ideas are correct|Avoid speaking with people she doesn't like to prevent her personal feelings from tarnishing interview insight
answers.definition: Look for extreme users to help figure out what future is already happening

answers.term: radio, Maggie is great at affective empathy, but struggles with cognitive empathy. Which of the following is Maggie likely to be good at handling? |Maggie gets a call from her best friend Bonnie whose dog just died. Bonnie asks her to come over because she needs a friend.|Maggie, a civilian, is interviewing military users who relate their experience with the product to experiences they had in their time overseas.|Maggie is tasked with preparing for a negotiation where it will be important to understand her opponent's way of thinking.|Maggie needs to understand the thought process behind a developer's experience with her product.
answers.definition: Maggie gets a call from her best friend Bonnie whose dog just died. Bonnie asks her to come over because she needs a friend.

answers.term: radio, Clare is designing a new product for a clothing company, and she is planning to hold a sensemaking discussion with her team. When she is holding the session, who should her and her team's focus be for the target audience of their potential product? |The majority of people - those who fall in the middle of the bell curve|The outliers at the extreme ends of the curve whose needs may be radically different from the norm|A general audience - it's not necessary to refine the audience just yet|The people in the middle of the bell curve and the outliers at each extreme
answers.definition: The people in the middle of the bell curve and the outliers at each extreme

answers.term: radio, Breanna has an idea she's very excited about. She believes this idea could help improve the speed at which clinics can operate, leaving people sitting in the wait room less, getting what they need, and leaving satisfied from their visit. Instead of going through the key process of sensemaking on her own, she plans to involve a team of other people. Why is this important? |Sensemaking in a team leaves less room for error as there are more people to work with.|She can uncover new insights and dig deeper than one ever could have individually.|It allows each individual to solidify their own ideas against other ideas.|Each person sharing their own ideas to others allows for correct thinking.
answers.definition: She can uncover new insights and dig deeper than one ever could have individually.

answers.term: radio, John is approaching the sensemaking phase of Design Thinking. He has noticed in the past that sensemaking can change innovators and their mindsets. Why is that? |They struggle to understand why users think and act as they do.|They are comfortable with ambiguity to discover deeper meanings.|They attempt to avoid conflict and try to get the "right" interpretation of data.|They don't reframe the definition of the problem and keep it simple.
answers.definition: They are comfortable with ambiguity to discover deeper meanings.

answers.term: radio, Jonah is working on a branding project for a skincare company. He arranges a meeting of stakeholders to view his team's designs in order to get their approval and alignment. A member of his team asks him why alignment is needed before moving forward. Why is alignment so important? |Keeping ideas suppressed when hearing others' views that seem better allow for further and quicker designing|It allows for certain controlled access and interactions which help generate ideas.|It allows everyone to explore each others' views and be open to the idea that their own perspective may be missing something.|It brings about conversations from leaders that keep the group small.
answers.definition: It allows everyone to explore each others' views and be open to the idea that their own perspective may be missing something.

answers.term: radio, Why is alignment so important?
answers.definition: It allows everyone to explore each others' views and be open to the idea that their own view may be missing something.

answers.term: radio, Kate is a senior leader in her firm and is planning to lead an alignment session. She invites her organization (about 45 people) to an alignment session to bring about inclusiveness and make sure all ideas are heard and taken note of when coming to an alignment. She does not attend the meeting as she has other conflicts, but is confident her team will produce a good result. What is the most important thing that Kate missed when setting up this meeting? |Kate included way too many people to be productive and get the desired results from alignment.|She believes in the "kumbaya effect" where people with differences will naturally join hands in spontaneous agreement and alignment.|Kate set the meeting up perfectly, bringing in everyone for inclusiveness.|She didn't show up to the meeting after setting it up. She should have moved it to a time she could be available.
answers.definition: She believes in the "kumbaya effect" where people with differences will naturally join hands in spontaneous agreement and alignment.

answers.term: radio, Teddy is attempting a new effective dialogue technique for his team. He connects his whole organization in dialogue in a retreat format. What term refers to this style of effective dialogue? |World Cafe|Appreciative Inquiry|Future Search|Democratic Dialogue

radio, Adam is a project lead working for an auto parts company. He has formed a group, and is striving to achieve alignment for an upcoming project that he would like to implement. What is a critical FIRST step for him that cannot be overlooked? |Make sure to form a large group of people in order to bring about the best ideas|Set some structure to the alignment meeting and make sure to have someone taking notes|Design and develop user stories and journey maps for the people they are designing for|Understanding and aligning on the definition of the problem and the needs for whom they are designing for
answers.definition: Understanding and aligning on the definition of the problem and the needs for whom they are designing for

answers.term: radio, Which of the following best describes perspective taking? |Removing boundaries driven by each members' own personal meaning to avoid different interests clashing|A group activity that requires people to come together, not only to understand each other, but to forge something collectively new|Understanding and acknowledging others' perspectives while sharing your own in a meaningful way|Starting with collective exploration of insights during sensemaking
answers.definition: Understanding and acknowledging others' perspectives while sharing your own in a meaningful way.

answers.term: radio, Tom is looking to expand his knowledge on design thinking practices and looking to add more to his playbook. He finds a few articles on the practice of perspective taking and begins to read them. He sees the importance of perspective taking, and plans to add it to his practice. Which of the following best describes perspective taking? |Removing boundaries driven by each members' own personal meaning to avoid different interests clashing|A group activity that requires people to come together, not only to understand each other, but to forge something collectively new|Understanding and acknowledging others' perspectives while sharing your own in a meaningful way|Starting with collective exploration of insights during sensemaking
answers.definition: Understanding and acknowledging others' perspectives while sharing your own in a meaningful way

answers.term: radio, Raj is a member of a design team at a sportswear company. He is looking to expand his knowledge on design thinking practices and finds articles on perspective making. Which of the following best describes perspective making? |Understanding and acknowledging others' perspectives while sharing your own in a meaningful way|An individual effort initiated during Immersion that is a key part of developing empathy|A group activity that requires people to come together, not only to understand each other, but to forge something collectively new|Removing boundaries driven by each members' own personal meaning to avoid different interests clashing
answers.definition: A group activity that requires people to come together, not only to understand each other, but to forge something collectively new

answers.term: radio, Ned wants to create an environment for his team to practice design thinking and alignment without making anyone feel uncomfortable. He writes out why dialogue and the emphasis on dialogue is important in these meetings in order to get alignment. Which of these is NOT an emphasis of dialogue? |inclusivity and an openness to being individually changed by the conversation|creating a formal process through negotiation|intention to act as a collective|willingness to share honestly and listen with an open mind
answers.definition: creating a formal process through negotiation

answers.term: radio, The purpose of diversity in the Emergence stage is to... |encourage the "boss effect."|come up with the "winning" idea.|identify new and better concepts that are superior to what any individual stakeholder could have brought into the conversation.|eliminate different views from being introduced to the solution-forming process.
answers.definition: identify new and better concepts that are superior to what any individual stakeholder could have brought into the conversation.

answers.term: radio, The idea that to adapt successfully to the diversity of challenges in our environment, we must (as a whole) have the same level of diversity represented in our experiences most accurately describes which of the following? |shout-out issue|goal of emergence|law of requisite variety|power of emptiness
radio, The process of selecting the least worst solution to which everyone will agree is called... |satisficing.|higher ordering.|innovating.|visualizing.
radio, The heart of the Imagining phase involves... |visualization.|brainstorming.|data analytics.|higher order solutions.
