You can learn more about the graded and practice items in the Course Overview . Activity Overview In this activity, you will identify project tasks by reviewing project and company documents. Then you will draft the project plan for Sauce & Spoon's tabletop menu tablets project. Scenario Review the scenario below. Then complete the step-by-step instructions. Peta, the new in-house project manager for Sauce & Spoon restaurants, has finished drafting the project charter for their tabletop menu tablets project. Her next step is to identify tasks to include in a project plan that will help her team reach the project's goals. To identify project tasks, Peta spends some time reviewing project documentation for the current tablet project. She also examines the project plan from a completed Sauce & Spoon project for information that could help the team complete the tablet rollout. Step-By-Step Instructions Step 1: Access the template Click the link to create a copy of the template. If you don't have a Google account, download the template directly from the attachment below. Link to template: Project Plan Template OR Download template: Activity Template_ Project plan XLSX File Step 2: Access the supporting materials The following supporting materials will help you complete this activity. Keep them open as you proceed to the next steps. Each link will open a new Coursera tab. Project Charter: Review your completed project charter from Week 1 Historical Project Plan Email Exchange: Tablet Logistics Note: To review supporting materials introduced in earlier activities, you can find them in the Resources section . Step 3: Make a list of 10 tasks Review the project charter, historical project plan, and email exchange and identify 10 tasks that might be required for the tablet rollout project. Identify at least one task from each supporting document. Remember that project tasks refer to activities that need to be accomplished within a set period of time, which eventually lead to the completion of a milestone.Remember that generative AI tools can be a great way to brainstorm! Then, add the tasks to the Task Brainstorm tab of your project plan in the Task column. As you add your tasks, ask yourself the following Guiding Tips and Questions: Are there multiple tasks implied by a single sentence? For example, "Launch a reservation system" implies that the team selected, installed, tested, and then launched the reservation system. Always ask yourself what decisions might need to be made before an action is taken and what testing might need to be done to verify the success of that action. These decisions and tests might also be considered tasks for the project plan. Step 4: Save your work Be sure to save the project plan you updated for this activity. You will revise and refine project artifacts, including the project plan, as you progress through the course. Pro Tip: Save the template Finally, be sure to save the template you used to complete this activity for further practice or to use in your own personal or professional projects. These templates will be useful as you put together a portfolio of project management artifacts that you can speak to in an interview to demonstrate your experience to potential employers. Activity Overview In this activity, you will create evaluation questions in order to help you determine if the project is meeting the quality standards you outlined. An evaluation question is a key question about the outcomes, impact, and/or effectiveness of your project or program. You will also create evaluation indicators to help you get the right information needed to answer the questions. Evaluation indicators define the specific type of data that needs to be collected. Scenario Review the scenario below. Then complete the step-by-step instructions. Now that the tablet test launch is complete, Peta wants to ensure that it leads to a successful rollout at both pilot locations. She does this by creating evaluation questions and indicators to measure the results of the test launch, and assess the project's progress at this stage. Step-By-Step Instructions Step 1: Access your draft Begin by opening the project plan draft that you worked on in the last activity, Add quality standards to your project plan. Step 2: Create evaluation questions Based on the quality standards you identified in the last activity, create 2-3 evaluation questions you would ask to assess the success of the tablet test launch. Add these questions under the Quality and Evaluation tab in your project plan, in the Evaluation Questions column. Remember, there are two main types of evaluation questions. There are questions that ask how you can make improvements, such as: How can we improve? What is working and what's not working? Which goals are being met? Who is benefiting? What are the most common participant reactions? There are also questions that help you measure and compare, such as: Were there unintended outcomes? What were the costs and benefits? Are there any lessons to be learned? Should we continue? A well-crafted evaluation question should provide you with valuable data. As you create your evaluation questions, consider the following: Does the question address stakeholder or user values, interests, and concerns? Does the question relate to the purposes of the project and of evaluation? Is the question worth answering and important for the project and beyond? Is the question practical and feasible to answer with available resources? Step 3: Add evaluation indicators Next, create an evaluation indicator for each evaluation question. Add your evaluation indicators under the Quality and Evaluation tab in your project plan, in the Evaluation Indicators column. Evaluation indicators state the specific type of data you need to collect to answer your evaluation questions. As you create your evaluation indicators, ask yourself the following questions: What do you want to measure or evaluate? The number of something? The level of satisfaction? Preferences? Demographic information like age, gender, or experience? Will the indicator demonstrate that you have reached the desired outcome? Will the indicator provide measurable evidence of meeting a goal? When should onboarding begin? | On the new hire's first day. | At the time of the offer for the position. | During the new hire's first week. | Timing isn't that important, just get it on the new hire's schedule soon.
answers.definition: At the time of the offer for the position.

answers.term: We want onboarding to be individualized. So it's best to make sure that the new employee is signed up ahead of time for all the appropriate groups to which the new hire belongs (like the women's leadership group, or the LGBT employee group, etc.). True or false? | True | False

It can be difficult to create an individualized onboarding process. But what is the most important thing to think of as you create your onboarding program? | Make sure you get the new hire paperwork done. | Introduce the new hire to the organization's leader. | Be intentional about designing the human relationship. | Make the process super fun.
answers.definition: Be intentional about designing the human relationship.

answers.term: What is the first step in getting ready for your new hire's first day? | Prepare yourself. | Talk with the new hire. | Get your team ready. | Set up a welcoming environment. | Talk with HR about paperwork.

Is it important to pre-schedule time with your new hire during the first week of employment? | Yes, put it on both your calendars. | If possible, but if emergencies come up try for some time in the first month. | No, just make sure you have a meeting with the new hire in the first month.
answers.definition: Yes, put it on both your calendars.

answers.term: It is important that the new hire not make mistakes as that will reflect poorly on his or her first performance review, true or false? | True | False

You want your team to be involved with the new hire onboarding process. But if there are concerns your team has with the new hire, they should do the following: | Keep it to themselves, this is a new employee and things are bound to get better. | Talk with the other team members about the concern to see if the concern is shared. | Bring the concern to you so you can help resolve it. | Talk directly with the new hire and explain how things are done on the team.
answers.definition: Bring the concern to you so you can help resolve it.

answers.term: What is the best way to be sure that you are ready for the new hire's first day? | Ask others to help. | Create and use an onboarding checklist. | Talk with human resources. | Ask the new hire what they need.
answers.definition: Create and use an onboarding checklist.

answers.term: Job satisfaction and employee engagement are the same thing. | True | False

A strong driver for both job satisfaction and employee engagement is: | Pay and benefits | The team of people you work with | Where the job is located | The employee relationship with the direct supervisor
answers.definition: The employee relationship with the direct supervisor

answers.term: Individual development plans must be designed for each individual, even when all your team members are working on the same projects and outcomes, true or false? | True | False
A sample Individual Development Plan (IDP) was discussed in this lesson. What was NOT one of the four parts of that sample IDP? | Goals | Strategies | Action Steps | Planning | Resources/Support

Which of the following are reasons why you should talk with your new hire about your organization's performance review system during the early days of onboarding? | Such a discussion will help the new hire know what is expected in the position. | Such a discussion will create a communication channel for you and the new hire. | Such a discussion helps both you and the new hire to think about what documentation you will want to collect for the review. | Such a discussion creates a sense of longevity with the organization for the new hire as they begin to think of the future early on in their career. | All of the above.

The toolset for performance management includes all of the following EXCEPT: | Setting clear expectations with the employee | Definition of managing people | Building development plans | Providing positive and corrective feedback
"Good performance management is the single largest contributor to organizational effectiveness." True or False. | True | False

Which of the following statistics is NOT accurate from the survey on performance management effectiveness? | 85% of employees focus on the "right" things defined by organization goals. See video 1.1.3 | 43% reported performance management process increased employee performance. | 51% said planning process needed work.
answers.definition: 85% of employees focus on the "right" things defined by organization goals.

answers.term: True or False: While there are many sources of culture difference in performance management, they are many key principles that are culture "neutral." | True | False
Which of the following was NOT listed in the lecture as an example of culture types? | Group | Collectivist | Individualistic
Which of the following is TRUE about performance reviews? | Reviews are strategic. | Reviews focus on individual development and ratings. | Reviews are a dynamic process.
answers.definition: Reviews focus on individual development and ratings.

answers.term: Which of the purposes listed for effective performance management systems would most likely be of use when terminations occur? | Legal | Strategic | Administrative | Rewards
Which of the following was listed as a design element for performance management systems? | Top Management buy in. | Frontline buy in. | Non comprehensive - used for non senior management positions
Workforce planning and and succession planning data is the only useful data form performance management systems. True or False? | True | False
Which of the following was not listed as an a external group impacted by an organizations performance management system? | Families. | Customers. | Suppliers. | Stockholders.
Which of the following is NOT part of strategic performance management? | Performance planning. | Multi-rater assessment. | The performance review. | Annual feedback sessions.

Which of the the following IS NOT a role of HR in the performance management planning process? | Ongoing feedback. | Conduct performance management training for managers. | Review job descriptions. | Developing performance standards.

As a manager you want to avoid the "perils" of of ineffective performance management. Which of the following is NOT a peril associated with specifically with managers? | Less motivated employees. | Lower stock price. | More turnover in the department. | Unfair / inconsistent performance ratings.

Performance management training may address performance improvement plans and individual development plans. The difference between the two is that improvement plans deal with a current performance deficiency, while the individual development deals with growth. True or False? | True | False

In the Case Study in the video regarding the strategy change in financial institution, the role of HR in implementing the new strategy was discussed. Which of the following actions was the role of the senior management team and NOT HR? | Conducted organizational SWOT analysis. | Revised training to incorporate new strategy. | Revised job descriptions to incorporate new skills and job requirements associated with new strategy. | Revised recruiting to incorporate new strategy.

Which of the following is NOT part of a performance management mindset ? | Performance management should be viewed as bottom line issue. | Performance management is about development of employees. | Performance management should be viewed as an event.
answers.definition: Performance management should be viewed as an event.

answers.term: Performance reviews can only be formal reviews and should never be informal. True or false? | True | False

Which of the following should be a part of a general performance discussion? | Add new data to surprise the employee. | Set clear expectations for the employee and the position. | Discuss both past and future behavior. | Contain a recap of prior discussions.
answers.definition: Set clear expectations for the employee and the position. | Discuss both past and future behavior. | Contain a recap of prior discussions.

answers.term: Organizations depend on performance review data for many reasons. Which of the follow is an example of an organizational use of performance review data? | individual compensation increases. | individual training plans. | individual development and growth plans. | leadership development and succession planning.

When doing a employee performance review, which of the following is important to make sure it part of the review? | Focus mostly on past behavior so the employee realizes what a great job they have done. | Inflate the rating or be vague so the employee will not be demotivated. | Delegate to the employee the task of determining how he/she will improve performance. | Have a fair amount of focus on the future, as part of the discussion.
answers.definition: Have a fair amount of focus on the future, as part of the discussion.

answers.term: Performance reviews should only be about rewarding employees. True or False | True | False

When you need to have a difficult feedback discussion, which of the following should be TRUE of that discussion? | Be sympathetic to the employee's issues. | Enhance self-esteem. | Include alternative behavioral options for the employee to improve upon.
answers.definition: Include alternative behavioral options for the employee to improve upon.

answers.term: "Feedback is like a shot" was talked about in the video. Why? | We get shots once a year. | Feedback, like a shot, should be given by a professional. | We love getting feedback! | Feedback helps us to get better.
answers.definition: Feedback helps us to get better.

answers.term: As a manager you want to get feedback from other sources (Multi rater feedback) with your sales employees who are located in store locations each with where there are three other employees. Which of the following sources would you want to make SURE to get feedback from? | Customers and peers. | Customers and employee. | Customers, peers and the employee. | Customers.

People who give multi rater feedback should do all of the following EXCEPT: | Provide feedback that includes behavioral examples. | Provide feedback on the employee's personality. | Provide performance that was observed. | Provide examples of positive behavior.
answers.definition: Provide feedback on the employee's personality.

answers.term: One of the easiest and most cost effective ways to build employee confidence, develop competence and improve performance is to give your employees feedback on a regular and ongoing basis. True or False? | True | False

Which of the following were described as intentional errors when rating employees? | Being an "easy grader." | Rating everyone the same. | Assigning additional "traits" to an employee. | Being a "tough grader."
answers.definition: Being an "easy grader." | Rating everyone the same. | Being a "tough grader."

answers.term: Which of the following are unintentional errors? | Recency / Primacy. | Varying standards. | Sampling error. | Strictness error.
answers.definition: Recency / Primacy. | Varying standards. | Sampling error.

answers.term: Which of the following are effective strategies to minimize legal issues in performance management? | Provide calibration training to managers who conduct reviews. | Provide training that contains insight on rater errors and why they occur. | Inflate employee ratings to make employees look good. | Have HR and/or senior managers provide oversight of final reviews.
answers.definition: Provide calibration training to managers who conduct reviews. | Provide training that contains insight on rater errors and why they occur. | Have HR and/or senior managers provide oversight of final reviews.

answers.term: Which of the following are tips for minimizing rater errors? | Managers Justify ratings. | Oversight by others in the organization (HR - Senior managers). | Hire managers who have experience. | Monitor across departments and manager for overall consistency.
answers.definition: Managers Justify ratings. | Oversight by others in the organization (HR - Senior managers). | Monitor across departments and manager for overall consistency.

answers.term: Providing training to employees who have performance issues is an effective way to minimize legal risk. True or false? | True | False
Which of the following was stated in video concerning culture and strategy? | Culture eats strategy for breakfast. | Strategy eats culture for breakfast.
"How we do things around here" is a definition of which of the following? | HR Processes. | Strategy. | Culture.
Which of the following would describe attributes of culture in an organization? | Mission. | Goals. | Corporate citizenship, norms and morés.
What is not one of the 3 R's of Civility from the lecture? | Restraint. | Reality. | Respect. | Responsibility.
Which of the following was not listed under the "R" of Restraint? | Active listening. | Acting on values. | Emotional regulation.
According to the statistic in the lecture, 50% of US employees have stated they were bullied or witnessed such behaviors. True or False? | True | False
Which of the following was listed an impact on teams in a culture of incivility? | Interpersonal Conflicts. | Increased anxiety. | Decreased individual performance. | Decreased job satisfaction.
One of the consequences of an uncivil culture is people are afraid to speak up for fear of consequences. True or False? | True | False
Which of the following is not a hard cost of incivility to organizations? | Increased absenteeism. | Increased turnover. | Decreased workers compensation claims.
A civil, positive culture can produce positive results that could be seen as a "dividend" to the organization. True of False? | True | False
Servant Leadership focuses on which of the following? | Coercion. | Values. | Scarcity.
In the cultural "audit," a gap analysis looks at the difference between your cultural vision and your desired vision. True or False? | True | False

In the "quilt of civility" one of the items was workplace design. Which of the following were mentioned as part of workplace design? | Cubes vs offices. | Geographic Locations. | What is on the walls in the organization.What is on the walls in the organization.
answers.definition: Cubes vs offices. | What is on the walls in the organization.What is on the walls in the organization.

answers.term: To create civility in a culture you must do which of the following? | Enforce it. | Let it occur naturally.
"Walk the talk" means: | Our deeds follow our words. | Management by Walking Around (MWA).
"Do unto others as they would have done unto themselves" was identified as: | The Golden Rule. | The Customer Rule. | The Platinum Rule.

According to the lesson, when looking at performance, we often use results _____________. | to infer behavior. | when behaviors are not easily observed. | to infer behavior and/or when behaviors are not easily observed.
answers.definition: to infer behavior and/or when behaviors are not easily observed.

answers.term: When defining performance we focus on: | Results. | Behaviors.
A bank teller knowing all of the products a bank offers is an example of ________? | Procedural Knowledge. | Declarative Knowledge. | Employee Motivation.

You have an employee you know has done a good job in the past and has received good reviews. The job has not changed but lately their performance has not been good as before. Using the concept from class of "diagnose before you prescribe," which of the following would you focus on? | Declarative Knowledge - I would send the employee to training. | Procedural Knowledge - I would have the employee review procedures. | Motivation - Coaching - I would have a discussion with the employee on why their performance has fallen off.
answers.definition: Motivation - Coaching - I would have a discussion with the employee on why their performance has fallen off.

answers.term: Which of the following was NOT listed as best HR practices in this lesson? | Corporate Branding. | Work/Life Balance. | Rewarding Employees. | Inclusive Environment.

Managers who are measuring an employee's punctuality, how well the employee works with others and the employee's communication skills are demonstrating which performance approach? | Behavior | Traits | Results
Information about the job, broad areas of responsibilities and day to day duties best describes which of the following? | Job Description | Accountabilities | Goals | Objectives

Which of the following is an example of a effective performance objective? | Increase Sales | Increase sales by 10% | Increase sales by 10% by end of quarter | Increase overall sales by 10% over last year by the end of this calendar year.
answers.definition: Increase overall sales by 10% over last year by the end of this calendar year.

answers.term: One of the characteristics of performance objectives is that they should be limited to 3 to 5 maximum. Why is this an important? | More objectives would make it difficult to convey a strong sense of priority for the desired objectives. | It is too hard to come up with more than three objectives.. | Employees don't like a lot of objectives because they have to work harder. | None of the above
answers.definition: More objectives would make it difficult to convey a strong sense of priority for the desired objectives.

answers.term: Which statement best describes the difference between a performance standards and performance objectives? | Performance standards effect all employees in a single position while objectives are unique to the individual. | There is no difference. | Performance standards are unique to the individual, objectives effect all employees in a single position.
answers.definition: Performance standards effect all employees in a single position while objectives are unique to the individual.

answers.term: In this type of comparative system, employees are rated according on a normal curve with only percentage of performers at the top, middle and bottom. | Forced distribution. | Simple rank order. | Paired comparison.
Gathering examples of performance in which employees performed very effectively or not effectively is known as: | Critical Incidents method. | Simple Ranking. | Essay.

If you were to select (in order) the best performer, then the worst, the second best and then the second worst until you met in the middle you would be using which of the following methods? | Alternating rank ordering. | Simple rank order. | Forced distribution. | MBO's.

As manager I want to make sure my employees are focused on their goals and aligned with corporate strategy. Which method would best meet my needs. | Essay. | Forced distribution. | MBO's. | None of the above.
Which of the methods has become a somewhat controversial method? | Essay. | Forced Distribution. | MBO's. | Simple rating.
A job description for administrative assistants may include "answering the telephone and transferring calls" under: | Job duties | KSAs | Job context | Job title
The process of producing a job description is called: | Job analysis | Job descriptioning | Job describing | Job evaluation

Which of the following statements about benchmarking is FALSE? | Ideally, benchmarks should match educational requirements of the organization's job with the educational requirements of the external benchmark's job. | The US Bureau of Labor Statistics produces estimates of pay in different occupations. | When some external jobs match best on job titles, and other external jobs match best on job descriptions, then it's better to benchmark on job titles rather than job descriptions. | Some external benchmarks are better than others, and when calculating the benchmark average, you may put extra weight on better benchmarks.
answers.definition: When some external jobs match best on job titles, and other external jobs match best on job descriptions, then it's better to benchmark on job titles rather than job descriptions.

answers.term: Suppose your organization wants to match pay on the external labor market. Which one of these statements is TRUE? | The typical job entrant without experience will begin below the market median pay for that job. | The typical job entrant without experience will begin above the market median pay for that job. | The typical job entrant without experience will begin at the market median pay for that job.
answers.definition: The typical job entrant without experience will begin below the market median pay for that job.

answers.term: Which of the following is NOT a best practice for compensation surveys, for the purposes of complying with anti-trust law? | Making sure that no one big survey respondent is the main driver of the benchmark data. | Making sure the data are sufficiently old. | Administering the survey yourself.

Suppose that a new technology makes coal mining much safer. What affect will this have on labor supply and labor demand? | Labor demand will increase | Labor supply will increase | Labor supply will decrease | The labor supply and labor demand curves will both change | Neither curve will change | Labor demand will decrease

Suppose that several large companies simultaneously announce that they're going to invest heavily in public infrastructure, raising the price of steel and iron ore. What will happen to the quantity and price (wages) for iron miners? | Labor demand will shift right: iron miners' wages will rise and the quantity of miner will increase. | Labor supply will shift left: iron miners' wages will increase and the quantity of miners will decrease. | Labor demand will shift left: iron miners' wages will decline and the quantity of miners will also decline. | The labor supply and labor demand curves will both change | The labor supply curve will shift right: iron miners' wages will decrease and the quantity of miners will increase. | Neither curve will change
answers.definition: Labor demand will shift right: iron miners' wages will rise and the quantity of miner will increase.

answers.term: Which of the following is TRUE about pay ranges? | The pay range will give the difference in pay between the least paid person in a grade and the second-least paid person in the pay grade. | The pay range will give the difference in pay between the least-paid person in a grade and the most-paid person in that grade. | The pay range will give the difference in pay between the lowest grade and the highest grade. | The pay range will give the difference in pay between two adjacent grades.
answers.definition: The pay range will give the difference in pay between the least-paid person in a grade and the most-paid person in that grade.

answers.term: When we draw our salary structure, a movement from left to right corresponds to: | A pay reduction, as you're getting a reduction in pay within the same grade. | A promotion, as you're getting promoted from a low grade to a higher grade. | A demotion, as you're getting demoted from a high grade to a lower grade. | A raise, as you're getting an increase in pay within the same grade.
answers.definition: A promotion, as you're getting promoted from a low grade to a higher grade.

answers.term: Which of the statements about pay policy lines are TRUE? | They are only used to benchmark pay for the middle grades, and are not used to determine pay at high or low grades. | They go through the tops of the pay ranges. | They go through the midpoints of the pay ranges. | They go through the bottoms of the pay ranges.
answers.definition: They go through the midpoints of the pay ranges.

answers.term: The pay rates for the jobs that you benchmark are called: | The pay structure's grades. | The pay structure's ranges. | The pay structure's pay policy rates. | The pay structure's control rates.

Which of the following statements about merit-based raise criteria are TRUE? | Merit-based raise criteria would typically give the largest raises to people low in the pay range, and with high evaluations. | Merit-based raise criteria would typically give the largest raises to people high in the pay range, and with high evaluations. | Merit-based raise criteria cannot avoid paying people above the maximum of the pay range.
answers.definition: Merit-based raise criteria would typically give the largest raises to people low in the pay range, and with high evaluations.

answers.term: Which of the following pay structures pays employees a premium for additional occupational licenses and education? | Competency-based structures | Skills-based structures | Job-based structures

Which of the following is a purpose of broadbanding? | Flexibility in lateral job assignments. | Flexibility in pay. | Flexibility in allowing multiple career ladders. | All of the above. | None of the above.
Employees who perform well are given raises. This is an example of a performance evaluation being tied to which element of the pay mix? | LTIs | Base pay | Non-Monetary | STIs | Benefits and Perks
A good performance evaluation can lead to a boost in any of the following EXCEPT? | MBOs | STIs | Benefits and Perks | LTIs | Base pay

Suppose a company decides to separate performance evaluations from raises. Which of the following is a common reason that a company would do so? | The company is concerned that tying pay to evaluations can impede the ability of evaluations to serve as a coaching tool. | The company is concerned that tying pay to performance evaluation makes it difficult for managers and employees to communicate openly about development goals. | Tying pay to performance evaluations encourages poor performers to stay.
answers.definition: The company is concerned that tying pay to evaluations can impede the ability of evaluations to serve as a coaching tool.

answers.term: Managers conducting performance evaluations tend to overweight instances that occurred in the last week more than those that happened six months ago. This is an example of what kind of bias? | Halo | Anchoring | Recency | Primacy | Horn | Spillover

In advance of a measurement period, a performance evaluation sets specific performance targets for employees, and ties pay to the achievement of those targets. This evaluation is an example of | Behaviorally-Anchored Rating Scale (BARS) | Management by Objectives (MBO) | A Realistic evaluation | Critical Incidents evaluation
Which of the following is NOT an example of a Key Performance Indicator? | Units produced | Year-end bonus | Average customer service score | Total dollar value of sales generated

A factory line worker is paid a piecerate, or a rate per unit he or she produces. When the materials and components that the line worker receives are faulty, the line worker's performance suffers. This is an example of the | Measurement problem | Alignment problem | Control problem | Metering problem

A call center wants to identify how many calls a customer service representative should take in a given hour. To do so, they use historical data, finding that a customer service representatives can be expected to service an average of six calls per hour. By benchmarking productivity, they are trying to solve | The control problem | The metering problem | The alignment problem | The measurement problem
What is the relationship between pay and performance when a job only pays a base rate, without STIs? | Accelerated | Flat | Linear (positive slope) | Linear (negative slope)

Which of the following statement is TRUE? | A share is only valuable if its price goes up. | A dividend of "$1 per share" means you need to pay $1 to purchase a share of the stock. | Both of the above. | None of the above.

Which of the following definitions is correct? | The vesting period represents the period of time over which the options become allowed to be exercised. | The strike price is the market price of the stock on the date that the employee exercises the option to purchase the stock.
answers.definition: The vesting period represents the period of time over which the options become allowed to be exercised.

answers.term: Which of the following statements about non-qualified stock options (NQSOs) is accurate? | Employers can deduct NQSOs as a business expense, employees do not pay taxes when they exercise NQSOs. | Employers cannot deduct NQSOs as a business expense, employees do pay taxes when they exercise NQSOs. | Employers cannot deduct NQSOs as a business expense, employees do not pay taxes when they exercise NQSOs. | Employers can deduct NQSOs as a business expense, employees do pay taxes when they exercise NQSOs.
answers.definition: Employers can deduct NQSOs as a business expense, employees do pay taxes when they exercise NQSOs.

answers.term: Which of the following is sometimes referred to as Golden Handcuffs? | bonuses | commissions | stock options | pensions
The differences between the stock price and the stock option's strike price is: | The time value | The intrinsic value | The vesting period

Employees who receive high performance evaluations for their prior year's accomplishments are awarded a fixed cash award. This is an example of tying evaluations to what element of the pay mix? | Base pay | Short Term Incentives | Perks | Non-Monetary | Long Term Incentives
Which of the following are examples of a Key Performance Indicators? | Units produced | Total dollar value of sales generated | Average customer service score | Year-end bonus
answers.definition: Units produced | Total dollar value of sales generated | Average customer service score

answers.term: Use the website http://www.dol.gov/whd/minwage/america.htm to look up minimum wages in the United States on January 1st, 2016. Which of the following would be true of employers and workers covered by the Fair Labor Standards Act? | Employers in Alabama must pay workers more than the federal rate of $7.25 per hour. | Employers in Alabama must pay workers at least the federal rate of $7.25 per hour. | Employers in Alabama may pay workers $5 per hour.
answers.definition: Employers in Alabama must pay workers at least the federal rate of $7.25 per hour.

answers.term: Which of the following requires employers to bargain in good faith over wages with workers' elected bargaining representative? | FLSA | NLRA | EEO | FMLA

Which person may be paid a salary? | Someone making $400 per week, whose job duties exempt them from the FLSA. | Someone making $800 per week, whose job duties exempt them from the FLSA. | Someone making $400 per week, whose job duties DO NOT exempt them from the FLSA. | Someone making $800 per week, whose job duties DO NOT exempt them from the FLSA. | None of the above.
answers.definition: Someone making $800 per week, whose job duties exempt them from the FLSA.

answers.term: Suppose that you're analyzing jobs for Crescendo Coffee, a major coffee retail chain. Assuming each of these people pass the salary test, which person is least likely to be exempted from the FLSA? | A district manager for the New England area. | The Chief Human Resource Officer. | A shift supervisor who primarily serves as a barista, and sometimes supervises one other employee. | A network engineer who maintains the computer systems.
answers.definition: A shift supervisor who primarily serves as a barista, and sometimes supervises one other employee.

answers.term: Which of the following statements is TRUE of an administrative assistant? | Their job is exempt from the FLSA. | They would need to be paid the minimum wage, but not overtime. Their job duties are not exempt from the FLSA. | They would need to be paid overtime, but not a minimum wage. Their job duties are not exempt from the FLSA.
answers.definition: They must be paid minimum wage and overtime. Their job duties are not exempt from the FLSA.

answers.definition: Six weeks paid leave for childbirth or adoption

answers.term: There are a several reasons firms use employer-sponsored pension plans. Mark the best answer | They're cheaper for firms to provide than for workers | They attract the right kind of worker | They're motivational symbolic benefits | They're cheaper for firms to provide than for workers and they enjoy returns to scale | They provide benefits to firms

answers.definition: Before announcing a furlough, I would first conduct a thorough audit of the financial situation to determine the exact length and scope of the furlough required. My recommendations for who will be furloughed would be based on objective, business-related criteria such as job function criticality, seniority (following last-in, first-out or merit-based protocols), and department-specific impacts to ensure equity and avoid discriminatory bias. Regarding compliance, I would ensure full adherence to the WARN Act if the scale meets federal or state thresholds, review employment contracts and collective bargaining agreements, ensure compliance with the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) regarding pay and classification, and verify that the selection process aligns with Title VII of the Civil Rights Act to prevent disparate impact.

answers.term: undefined, How would you announce the furlough to workers? What information would you share? |
answers.definition: The announcement would be handled with transparency, empathy, and professionalism, ideally through a mix of a company-wide town hall meeting followed by individual 1-on-1 meetings for those directly affected to maintain dignity. I would provide a written notice detailing the start and expected end date of the furlough, information regarding the continuation of benefits or loss thereof, instructions on how to file for unemployment insurance, and contact information for HR to address specific questions. Clear communication about the business necessity of the decision is crucial to maintain trust and morale for the workforce remaining on the job.

answers.term: This week you learned about the neurological pathways and activity areas of the brain that support thinking more creatively about the future. One of the most important neurological activities in thinking about the future is "scene construction." During scene construction, the brain creates a vivid movie or 3D virtual reality in your mind's eye. It allows you to "look around" and immerse yourself in a simulated scene, whether it's something that you're remembering or something you're imagining could happen in the future. What is another term for this neurological activity? | Performance monitoring | Memory and simulation | Mentalizing

Another important neurological activity that happens when we think about the future is that we try to simulate how other people might feel and what they might do. This activity is a way for our own brain to "get inside someone else's mind." That why it's called: | Mentalizing | Performance monitoring | Memory and simulation

A third neurological activity that happens when we think about the future is a kind of "scanning" of the future for possible opportunities to make choices and take actions that serve our own personal goals. What is this called? | Performance monitoring | Mentalizing | Memory and simulation

If you want to build up all of the neurological pathways that support these 3 important activities - memory and simulation, mentalizing and performance monitoring - you can practice the "magic triangle" of simulation. What are the 3 habits that make up this magic triangle? Pick three answers only. | Remembering the past exactly as it was | Remembering the future as if it has already happened | Predicting the past, and how it could have been different | Predicting the future, and explaining why it will be that way | Hard empathy, or imagining yourself in situations you've never directly experienced | Easy empathy, or experiencing other people's feelings in familiar situations as if it were happening to you
answers.definition: Remembering the future as if it has already happened | Predicting the past, and how it could have been different. | Hard empathy, or imagining yourself in situations you've never directly experienced.

answers.term: There's a region of the brain that fires up whenever you register something as important to you, personally. It says, "Hey! This matters to YOU! It's about YOU! Pay attention!" What is this region called? | Medial PreFrontal Cortext | Hippocampus | Temporal Lobe | Amygdala

What does this same part of the brain do, for most people, when they imagine themselves in a far future - say, 10 years out or more? | It acts like they're thinking about a complete stranger, someone who doesn't matter to them at all. | If they're in a good mood, it fires up and says "Hey! Pay attention!" If they're bored, frustrated, or angry, it doesn't react. | It fires up and says "Hey! This is important! Pay attention!"
answers.definition: It acts like they're thinking about a complete stranger, someone who doesn't matter to them at all.

answers.term: What's the result of this part of the brain's behavior, when it comes to imagining your future self? | It's easier to predict what you will do and harder to predict what other people will do in the future. As a result, you lose empathy for others and focus only on your own needs and goals. | It's hard to have empathy for your future self. As a result, you make decisions that feel good in the short run but are maybe not-so-good in the long run. | If you spend too much time thinking about your future self, you can become disoriented. You may become confused about what is realistic or possible and set unrealistic goals for yourself.
answers.definition: It's hard to have empathy for your future self. As a result, you make decisions that feel good in the short run but are maybe not-so-good in the long run.

answers.term: This week, you learned about 3 different areas of simulation innovation. One area of innovation is creating realistic video or audio of a real person saying something they've never actually said, or doing something they've never actually done. These videos and audio recordings are based on machine intelligence. An AI creates an authentic-seeming "fake" based on real, previous videos and audio recordings. So they are a hybrid of "real" and "faked." What does futurist Jamais Cascio call these new kinds of half-real simulations? | A "simtainer" | "Simulacra" | Haptics

Another area of simulation innovation is the use of shipping containers to create a portable Virtual Reality environment that can easily be set up, moved, and re-installed anywhere in the world. Futurists are using these spaces to imagine how real shipping containers, an important and underutilized part of the global infrastructure, might be used in the future. What is this project/technology called? | Simtainers | Simulacra | Haptics

The third simulation technology explored this week is technology that simulates touch. It allows you to have a physical sensation of touching a virtual object, or being touched by a virtual object. This can include anything from simulated hugs via video chat to phone vibrations that feel like raindrops falling on your hand. What is this technology field called? | Simtainers | Simulacra | Haptics

It's not hard to imagine negative consequences of simulacra technologies. Convincingly faked videos or faked audio created through AI machine learning will almost certainly lead to new forms disinformation, propaganda, and new kinds of bullying and harassment. But your reading this week identifies several possible positive uses of the technologies. Which example stands out to you as the most legitimately useful application? The author identifies some of the earliest known images of the future, ones that go much further back in human culture than the science fiction films and tv series and the modern dystopians novels often named as examples. Which of these are considered early "images of the future?" (multiple correct answers) | The City of God by St. Augustine | Plato's Politeia, also known as The Republic | Thomas More's Utopia
answers.definition: The City of God by St. Augustine | Plato's Politeia, also known as The Republic | Thomas More's Utopia

answers.term: Think back to the many different images of the future you have personally consumed via television, movies, comics, novels, religious texts, political speeches, advertisements and more over your life. Which ones would you say have made the biggest impression on YOU personally? Which anxieties about the future, or which hopes for the future, did these images help cultivate and nurture in you? Take some time to list any images of the future that leap to mind, and then make some notes or bullet points about which hopes and worries resonated with you most. This exercise can help you understand what pre-existing feelings YOU bring to your futures work, and how YOU might want to help ease society's anxieties or spark society's hope for the future. This final question is a personal reflection. There are no right or wrong answers; whatever you share will automatically be graded as correct. Use this question to reflect on what you learned this week and to make a more personal connection with the material. |
answers.definition: e many different images of the future you have personally consumed via television, movies, comics, novels, religious texts, political speeches, advertisements

answers.term: What's an artifact from the future? | An artist's rendering of an everyday object, physical or digital, that might exist in the future. | A short story that includes many vivid details about what the future might be like. | A scientific piece of evidence that strongly suggests how the future is most likely to turn out.
answers.definition: An artist's rendering of an everyday object, physical or digital, that might exist in the future.

answers.term: What's the relationship between an artifact from the future and a future forecast? | A forecast predicts what the future will most probably be like. An artifact is a piece of evidence that supports the prediction. | A forecast describes, generally, the world we might live in someday and how it could be different from today. An artifact is a new kind of object that might exist in that future. | A forecast is a description of a possible future and how it's different from today. An artifact is a specific, concrete, measurable outcome that can tell us: "Has this forecast come true yet, or not?"
answers.definition: A forecast describes, generally, the world we might live in someday and how it could be different from today. An artifact is a new kind of object that might exist in that future.

answers.term: What are some of the benefits of creating artifacts from the future? | It makes the future more "real" and "tangible" to our imagination. | It can spark thought and conversations about the future, especially for people who don't ordinarily think about the far future. | It can blur the line between "today" and "tomorrow" in a way that provokes strong emotional reactions.
answers.definition: It makes the future more "real" and "tangible" to our imagination. | It can spark thought and conversations about the future, especially for people who don't ordinarily think about the far future. | It can blur the line between "today" and "tomorrow" in a way that provokes strong emotional reactions.

answers.term: This week you read a Climate Action Report from the Institute for the Future. This quiz is about those 8 opportunity zones. If you need to refresh your memory: Page 5 of the reading describes the zones and Page 6 includes signals of change and scenarios from the 8 zones. This quiz is a personal reflection. There are no right or wrong answers. Your answers will automatically be marked "correct", whatever you say or choose. Use this quiz as an opportunity to reflect on what you've read and to make a more personal connection with the material. When you think of the 8 zones of opportunity for climate action, which ONE do you feel YOU would most likely take action in, sometime during the next decade? Pick the one you see the strongest fit with your values, interests, skills, resources and abilities. (And if you personally do not believe you will take any climate action in the next decade, feel free to choose that response.)
answers.definition: I do not believe that I personally will take any action to prevent or help others adapt to climate change in the future.

answers.term: What's one way YOU personally can see yourself taking climate action, in the zone of opportunity you chose, in the next 10 years? If you were to spend, for example, 100 hours helping prevent or adapt to climate change in the future - what would you be doing? (A few sentences of reflection are fine! And if you cannot imagine yourself doing anything to prevent or help others adapt to climate change in the future, please say so and what, if anything, might change that decision.) Again - this quiz is a personal reflection. There are no right or wrong answers. Your answers will automatically be marked "correct", whatever you say or choose. Use this quiz as an opportunity to reflect on what you've read and to make a more personal connection with the material.
answers.definition: ne way YOU personally can see yourself

answers.term: This week, you learned about a number of projects designed to help local communities think about the future, together. What about you?

answers.term: radio, Using the information of a hotel client's interview, written below, please select which of the options best exemplifies the touchpoints that represent the potential bottleneck for the family to move from the Purchase to the Loyalty phase of the purchase funnel. "Let's look at one family we interviewed, Peter and Anne from Madrid. They are a young couple in their 30s with 2 young children. They travel mostly within Spain by car, and like to go to places where there is lots to do for the kids, but also fun for him and his wife. They don't expect to spend a lot of time in the room, so he looks for hotels that have a convenient location, good rates and dependable service. What he really appreciates are small extras for the kids, and rooms that feel updated. They had set their sight on going to Valencia, because of the existence of both beach and the Oceanographic site. Peter asked a colleague from work who had recently visited Valencia, and he recommended our client's hotel. Peter immediately went online, looked at the hotels website pictures, and once he got approval from Anne, he decided to go ahead and book. It took him 45 minutes browsing through different booking engines to actually make the reservation, because pricing was different in every website, which really annoyed him. Let's fast forward to the actual arrival at the hotel. After the long drive, Peter and Anne began their check in process and the kids were roaming around the lobby playing with the luggage. Anne got really nervous that they would knock down some vases that are part of the décor. Once finished the check in process, they took the elevator up to their rooms, only to find out that they weren't connecting rooms. Annoyed, Peter went downstairs and after a long discussion with the reception clerk, he came up with the keys to connecting rooms. When they entered the rooms, the décor was updated, but the bed was hard as wood, and the bathroom had no bathtub (for the kids) and the shower hadn't been updated in a while. Let's Fast forward again to their departure day. Early in the morning, they received an envelope with the bill under their door. After revising it, Peter realizes that there were some minibar charges that weren't theirs. He went downstairs to reception to find a long cue. During this wait, he decides to write a review of the hotel on the Internet. After 15 minutes and a bit of discussion, he is finally able to sort out the bill and complete the check-out process." |Word of mouth, Hotel's web site, and the lobby.|The vases in the lobby, the connecting rooms, the bill.|Online booking, Bed, Shower, Reception staff for check in and check out, online review.|The elevator, the cue in the lobby, the bathtub.|None of the above.
