They may be able to self-improve by learning from data.C. They are exciting and captivating to many people.D. They can displace workers by performing their jobs more efficiently.
answers.definition: They can automate very complex operations.  B. They may be able to self-improve by learning from data.

answers.term: Management asks someone to do a data-related task. Which of the following would likely be ethically problematic? (Select two.)A. Aggregate data together.B. Change data to another format.C. Manipulate data or alter its interpretation.D. Delete any erroneous data.
answers.definition: Manipulate data or alter its interpretation.  D. Delete any erroneous data.

answers.term: Which of the following describe important aspects in the role of an ethical AI engineer? (Select two.)A. Building and maintaining computational hardware.B. Writing new equations to express intelligence.C. Keeping up with the latest developments and vulnerabilities.D. Cleaning and sorting data, and auditing for bias.
answers.definition: Keeping up with the latest developments and vulnerabilities.  D. Cleaning and sorting data, and auditing for bias.

answers.term: Which of the following, by itself, qualifies as personally identifiable information (PII)?A. Temperature readings for an office buildingB. A user's customer ID in an online ordering systemC. System events added to a logD. A user's home address

Why are groups like race and religion considered protected classes?A. These groups have been used as the basis for wholesale discrimination.B. These groups can be used to personally identify someone.C. People use these groups as the basis for their identities.D. Organizations are legally not allowed to collect information about these groups.
answers.definition: These groups have been used as the basis for wholesale discrimination.

answers.term: Which of the following describes an opt-out policy in regards to the collection of private data?A. Data about the user is always collected, regardless of the user's consent.B. Data about that user isn't collected until that user explicitly states you are allowed to.C. Data about the user is never collected, regardless of the user's consent.D. Data about the user is automatically collected unless that user explicitly states that you should not do so.
answers.definition: Data about the user is automatically collected unless that user explicitly states that you should not do so.

answers.term: Which of the following are key principles of privacy by design? (Select two.)A. Organizations must incorporate privacy protections throughout the project lifecycle.B. Organizations must keep the focus of privacy protections on the business rather than the user.C. Organizations must not expose the operational practices and technologies used to protect user privacy.D. Organizations must be proactive in protecting against privacy risks, not reactive.
answers.definition: Organizations must incorporate privacy protections throughout the project lifecycle.  D. Organizations must be proactive in protecting against privacy risks, not reactive.

answers.term: What is the purpose of differential privacy?A. To only allow certain parties to access certain portions of the data.B. To enable parties to share private data without revealing individuals represented in the data.C. To remove the direct identifiers that can be used to identify individuals.D. To ensure the data is completely confidential and cannot be read by unauthorized parties.
answers.definition: To enable parties to share private data without revealing individuals represented in the data.

answers.term: Which of the following describes the concept of liability?A. Answering for one's actions to an authority figure.B. Taking ownership of an assigned task.C. The legal responsibility for one's actions.D. The moral duty one has to take action.
answers.definition: The legal responsibility for one's actions.

answers.term: What does it mean to call a click-through agreement a "contract of adhesion"? | Both parties are legally bound by the agreement. | Both parties are equally responsible for ensuring the agreement is adhered to. | One party is forced into a "take-it-or-leave-it" situation. | One party is forced into using the service after agreeing.
answers.definition: One party is forced into a "take-it-or-leave-it" situation.

answers.term: Which of the following is a type of technology contract that establishes the goals of both parties and describes how those goals will be achieved?A. Software as a Service (SaaS)B. Service-level agreement (SLA)C. Terms of Service (ToS)D. End-user license agreement (EULA)

How does a smart contract differ from a traditional contract?A. Smart contracts eliminate the need for a central authority.B. Smart contracts guarantee that all parties are anonymous.C. Smart contracts serve a different purpose than traditional contracts.D. Smart contracts are more effective than traditional contracts.
answers.definition: Smart contracts eliminate the need for a central authority.

answers.term: How can a visual contract be easier to understand than a written contract?A. The use of pictures is more accessible to all people, whereas a written contract may be difficult for someone with a reading disability to understand.B. The use of pictures without any text makes it easier for most people to comprehend the details of a contract.C. The use of pictures with simple text makes it easier for the layperson to understand the details of a contract.D. The use of pictures explains the contract in greater detail than a written contract, making it easier for anyone to understand the particulars.
answers.definition: The use of pictures with simple text makes it easier for the layperson to understand the details of a contract.

answers.term: What causes bias?A. Biases are caused by the opinions of our families.B. Bias is biological, we are born with it.C. Bias is caused by the media.D. Biases are learned from our families, our social groups, and the media.
answers.definition: Biases are learned from our families, our social groups, and the media.

answers.term: What is the fundamental attribution error?A. When you believe your chances of experiencing something negative are lower and your chances of experiencing something positive are higher than others.B. When you believe your ideas are normal and that the majority of people agree with you.C. When you say your bad behavior is caused by the situation, but when other people display the same bad behavior, it is caused by a personality trait.D. When you incorrectly assume a cause and effect relationship for two correlated variables.
answers.definition: When you say your bad behavior is caused by the situation, but when other people display the same bad behavior, it is caused by a personality trait.

answers.term: Which of the following are actions that can help combat implicit bias? (Select three.)A. Interacting with diverse groups of people.B. Surrounding yourself with others who have similar experiences.C. Cultivating awareness of your own biases.D. Exposing yourself to "counter-stereotypical" examples.E. Obtaining your information from the same one or two media sources that your family and friends access.
answers.definition: Interacting with diverse groups of people.  C. Cultivating awareness of your own biases.  D. Exposing yourself to "counter-stereotypical" examples.

answers.term: When conducting an opinion poll, which of the following biases do you need to guard against the most when collecting your data?A. Correlation biasB. Modeling biasC. Misclassification biasD. Sampling bias
Which of the following is an example of a cognitive bias?A. Correlation biasB. Modeling biasC. Misclassification biasD. Anchoring bias

Are criminal justice risk assessments race-neutral?A. No, the data is biased as it reflects historical bias.B. Yes, technology in itself is not racist.C. Yes, algorithms replace human judgement and they are unbiased.D. No, it is designed with intention to be unfair.
answers.definition: No, the data is biased as it reflects historical bias.

answers.term: Which type of bias causes people to trust an automated decision-making system (ADS) over a human's decision? | Complacency bias | Automation bias | Confirmation bias | Implicit bias

How can confirmation bias impact us socially? (Select two.)A. It can prevent us from being social with other people.B. It can impede socio-political cooperation.C. It can lead to a diverse set of friends.D. It can lead to groupthink, which can in turn halt forward progress.
answers.definition: It can impede socio-political cooperation.  D. It can lead to groupthink, which can in turn halt forward progress.

answers.term: Which of the following describes an illusory-correlation bias?A. When you incorrectly assume a correlation because there is an illusory confounding variable.B. When you correlate variables that do not exist in your data set.C. When you correlate a variable with a confounding variable.D. When you incorrectly assume a cause and effect relationship because two variables are correlated.
answers.definition: When you incorrectly assume a correlation because there is an illusory confounding variable.

answers.term: Which of the following is one explanation for why cognitive biases exist?A. We use them to help remember things.B. We receive too much information and are overloaded.C. They are taught to us in school.D. They help us think logically instead of emotionally.
answers.definition: We receive too much information and are overloaded.

answers.term: Which of the following is a formative ethics theory that states that maximizing happiness is the primary standard for determining what is right or wrong?A. Categorical imperativeB. UtilitarianismC. DeontologyD. Virtue ethics

Which of the following statements are promoted by the categorical imperative? (Select three.)A. Act in such a way that your actions may become a universal law.B. You have a moral duty to choose your actions based on their potential outcomes.C. Each person must use reason to will moral laws.D. Don't treat people as a means to an end; treat them always as an end.
answers.definition: Act in such a way that your actions may become a universal law.  C. Each person must use reason to will moral laws.  D. Don't treat people as a means to an end; treat them always as an end.

answers.term: Which of the following statements accurately describes the philosophical concept of predeterminism?A. All events, past, present, and future, are determined in advance.B. All future events are determined by preceding events, as in a chain, but human beings may still be able to interfere with this chain of events.C. Human beings are able to make choices whose outcomes are not already determined.D. All events are predestined to happen by a supernatural force.
answers.definition: All events, past, present, and future, are determined in advance.

answers.term: How do norms differ from morals?A. Morals involve value judgments; norms do not.B. Norms are universal to all cultures; morals are not.C. Norms form the basis for morals.D. Morals are collective; norms are more personal.
answers.definition: Morals involve value judgments; norms do not.

answers.term: Which of the following are consequences of saying that someone or something has moral agency? (Select two.)A. The moral agent is capable of determining right and wrong.B. The moral agent can be held responsible for their actions.C. The moral agent acts in a morally correct manner.D. The moral agent follows a deontological code of ethics.
answers.definition: The moral agent is capable of determining right and wrong.  B. The moral agent can be held responsible for their actions.

answers.term: Why is deciding how to act using moral reasoning not always a feasible goal for human beings?A. Most people are not educated on normative ethical theories and therefore cannot perform true moral reasoning.B. Moral reasoning is too complicated to apply to a real-world situation.C. Moral reasoning has few tangible benefits for most people.D. Human decision making is often influenced by emotion and not logic.
answers.definition: Human decision making is often influenced by emotion and not logic.

answers.term: Which of the following statements are true regarding the purpose of moral psychology? (Select two.)A. Moral psychology seeks to understand why people act morally or immorally.B. Moral psychology seeks to understand how the human mind develops morality.C. Moral psychology seeks to understand the nature of what it means to be moral.D. Moral psychology seeks to understand what the best way to act morally is.
answers.definition: Moral psychology seeks to understand why people act morally or immorally.  B. Moral psychology seeks to understand how the human mind develops morality.

answers.term: Which of the following is an example of applied ethics?A. Professional ethicsB. Moral relativismC. Virtue ethicsD. Pluralism

Your organization has developed an AI system that recommends treatments for hospital patients. Some questions have been raised about the ethics of how these treatments are determined. What applied ethics domain do these concerns fall under?A. Environmental ethicsB. Business ethicsC. BioethicsD. Engineering ethics

What does it mean to say that human rights are inalienable? (Select two.)A. Inalienable rights are inherent in all human beings.B. Inalienable rights cannot be taken away except in extreme circumstances.C. Inalienable rights are conditional.D. Inalienable rights are derived from tradition.
answers.definition: Inalienable rights are inherent in all human beings.  B. Inalienable rights cannot be taken away except in extreme circumstances.

answers.term: What does "ethics by design" mean? | A creative design approach as the focus for ethics. | A reference to the framework set forth by IEEE's Ethically Aligned Design. | An approach in which ethics is considered from the initial design stage. | A reference to one of the tenets of engineering activism.
answers.definition: An approach in which ethics is considered from the initial design stage.

answers.term: Which of the following describes why explainability is important?A. It is necessary so that internal stakeholders can understand how a system works.B. It provides accountability and trust.C. It provides interpretations of a system's actions.D. It enables you to explain a system for shareholder purposes.

Which of the following describes personhood?A. Personhood is often used to dictate how something is treated.B. Personhood is a concept that applies to narrow AI.C. Personhood is the legal protection provided to AI systems.D. Personhood is an individual's right to freedom.
answers.definition: Personhood is often used to dictate how something is treated.

answers.term: Which of the following describe how adopting ethical practices can be a strategic differentiator? (Select three.)A. It will encourage applicants to apply for your company.B. It will ensure you comply with regulations.C. It will support the development of strategic partnerships.D. It will reduce your business obligations toward customers and business partners.E. It will build customer trust.
answers.definition: It will encourage applicants to apply for your company.  C. It will support the development of strategic partnerships.  E. It will build customer trust.

answers.term: Which of the following best describes beneficence?A. Beneficence is a term coined by IBM that relates to their Green Horizons initiative in 2014.B. Beneficence is the promotion of efficient systems that perform rapidly and benefit companies.C. Beneficence is the promotion of well-being for moral agents like humans.D. Beneficence is the promotion of well-being, not just for moral agents like humans, but of animals, the environment, and societies.
answers.definition: Beneficence is the promotion of well-being, not just for moral agents like humans, but of animals, the environment, and societies.

answers.term: What is the difference between beneficence and non-maleficence?A. Beneficence refers to "do only good" and non-maleficence refers to "do no harm."Non-maleficence refers only to malevolent artificial general intelligence (AGI), while beneficence can refer to any "good" emerging technology.C. Beneficence is a less important goal for the field of AI than non-maleficence.D. Beneficence and non-maleficence are quite similar and often interchangeable.
answers.definition: Beneficence refers to "do only good" and non-maleficence refers to "do no harm."

answers.term: Which of the following are valid concerns regarding electronic personalities? (Select two.)A. That they would create unfair advantages, as not everyone has access to the same rights.B. That individuals would start applying for electronic personalities.C. That they will make it more difficult to access information.D. That they would absolve manufacturers of liability.
answers.definition: That they would create unfair advantages, as not everyone has access to the same rights.  D. That they would absolve manufacturers of liability.

answers.term: Which of the following are ways to participate in engineering activism? (Select two.)A. Follow a code of ethics.B. Perform all tasks required of you.C. Engage with the public.D. Follow ethics by design.
answers.definition: Follow a code of ethics.  C. Engage with the public.

answers.term: How can AI uphold justice?A. The more AI-based products being used in the justice system, the more justice can be upheld.B. AI systems can be designed from the start to help promote fairness and minimize bias.C. AI systems can replace human judges, who are often biased.D. AI can automate many of the clerical tasks involved in the justice system.
answers.definition: AI systems can be designed from the start to help promote fairness and minimize bias.

answers.term: Which of the following are examples of how AI can limit human autonomy? (Select two.)A. Weapon systems can limit human autonomy as humans may not have decision-making capability or understand the decision making.B. AI systems might impact certain vulnerable groups such as the elderly and children differently than the rest of the population, which could limit those groups' autonomy.C. AI systems can assist individuals with automated, repetitive, or dangerous tasks.D. AI systems can perform tasks that humans cannot, such as processing millions of data records in a matter of seconds.
answers.definition: Weapon systems can limit human autonomy as humans may not have decision-making capability or understand the decision making.  B. AI systems might impact certain vulnerable groups such as the elderly and children differently than the rest of the population, which could limit those groups' autonomy.

answers.term: Which school of philosophical thought primarily advocates for the greatest good for the greatest amount of people?A. Kantian ethicsB. UtilitarianismC. DeontologyD. Virtue ethics
Which type of entity are the OECD Principles on Artificial Intelligence mostly geared towards?A. Municipal governmentsB. Private corporationsC. National governmentsD. Individuals

Which of the following principles are most commonly cited in AI-based ethical frameworks?A. Happiness and spiritual contentmentB. Human control and autonomyC. Fairness and non-discriminationD. Transparency and explainability
Which of the following frameworks primarily promotes human rights?A. The Montreal DeclarationB. The Asilomar AI PrinciplesC. The Toronto DeclarationD. The Beijing AI Principles

Which of the following best describes capability caution as referenced in the Asilomar AI Principles?A. Should there be a greater reliance on AI, measures should be taken to ensure that humans are still capable of finding work.B. We should keep limits on on what artificial general intelligence (AGI) is capable of.C. If there is no understanding of the internal mechanisms of AI, then AI development should be halted.D. Given a lack of consensus, we should avoid strong assumptions regarding upper limits on future AI capabilities.
answers.definition: Given a lack of consensus, we should avoid strong assumptions regarding upper limits on future AI capabilities.

answers.term: Which of the following describes the principle of transparency in the context of AI systems?A. Transparency enables human observers to reproduce the decision-making process of an AI system.B. Transparency enables human observers to see inside the decision-making process of an AI system.C. Transparency enables human observers to tweak the decision-making process of an AI system.D. Transparency enables human observers to understand the decision-making process of an AI system.
answers.definition: Transparency enables human observers to see inside the decision-making process of an AI system.

answers.term: Which of the following is a case study that best represents the principle of professional responsibility?A. The Asilomar AI Principles' definition of capability cautionB. The American Medical Association's definition of AI as augmented intelligenceC. The Beijing AI Principles' tenets about the use of AID. The IEEE Ethically Aligned Design's discussion on classical ethics
answers.definition: The American Medical Association's definition of AI as augmented intelligence

answers.term: If you are attempting to build a new framework for the research and development (R&D) of AI, which of the following frameworks might you look at first for its emphasis in this area?A. The G20 AI PrinciplesB. The Montreal Declaration for a Responsible Development of Artificial IntelligenceC. The American Medical Association's definition of artificial intelligenceD. The Beijing AI Principles
In AI, the principle of privacy is most commonly referred to in the context of which of the following concepts?A. TransparencyB. Data protectionC. Human controlD. Personal protection

Which of the following describes an ethical framework?A. Ethical frameworks apply meta-ethical theories to everyday business operations.B. Ethical frameworks consolidate regulatory requirements for an industry.C. Ethical frameworks raise timeless ethical questions that are not easily put into action.D. Ethical frameworks seek to mitigate ethical concerns by creating actionable steps.
answers.definition: Ethical frameworks seek to mitigate ethical concerns by creating actionable steps.

answers.term: Why does the trolley problem pose an ethical predicament?A. The moral responsibility is split between you and the person controlling the trolley.B. You have to make a choice between two scenarios where choosing one leads to loss of life in the other.C. You as the actor don't have sufficient control over the circumstance.D. There are so many potential outcomes that it becomes difficult to choose one that is most ethical.
answers.definition: You have to make a choice between two scenarios where choosing one leads to loss of life in the other.

answers.term: Which of the following ethical considerations should have priority in an emergency situation like the use of contact-tracing solutions during a pandemic? (Select two.)A. PrivacyB. BiasC. ExplainabilityD. Accountability
In using AI-enabled solutions within the context of medical imaging analysis, which of the following is the most important ethical consideration?A. ExplainabilityB. PrivacyC. SecurityD. Bias

If an AI-enabled system enables addictive behavior, which of the following makes for the most compelling argument to stop development work on that system?A. The user will share more data with the system because of increased use.B. There is a lack of accountability on the part of the user since they overuse the service.C. The process for obtaining consent has not been made transparent to the user.D. The system, as designed, acts counter to the well-being of the users.
answers.definition: The system, as designed, acts counter to the well-being of the users.

answers.term: Why do smart toys raise additional ethical concerns over those that are raised in the course of other products and services that use AI?A. Children are more susceptible to manipulation and therefore need extra protective measures.B. The smart toys store personal data on the device, which can be stolen.C. It is difficult to obtain informed consent for the use of the smart toy.D. They are used in the privacy of homes rather than in public settings, like other products or services.
answers.definition: Children are more susceptible to manipulation and therefore need extra protective measures.

answers.term: Which of the following software development principles is essential in the real-world deployment of AI-enabled software applications in critical scenarios like self-driving cars?A. Robustness to adversarial examplesB. Continuous integration and deployment of patch updatesC. Version control of the AI models deployedD. Architectural design analysis

Which of the following is the most important argument in favor of content moderation in online platforms?A. It prevents the spread of disinformation that can cause harm to vulnerable populations.B. It helps uphold freedom of expression for everyone and doesn't give anyone special rights.C. It creates adequate incentives for everyone to share their opinions.D. It prevents the development of monopolies in terms of content creators.
answers.definition: It prevents the spread of disinformation that can cause harm to vulnerable populations.

answers.term: Why is the question of robot rights and emancipation one that isn't as important as addressing issues of bias, privacy, transparency, and other principles discussed in the various ethical frameworks? | Robots are mechanical instruments and therefore don't deserve to have rights. | There is no legal precedent for granting rights to entities that are not humans. | Humans are anthropocentric and don't want to extend rights to other sentient entities. | These rights necessitate that robots become sentient entities, which is currently not feasible.
answers.definition: These rights necessitate that robots become sentient entities, which is currently not feasible.

answers.term: Which of the following is the most important ethical consideration regarding technical developments like deepfakes?A. They take away monetization opportunities, leaving individuals unfairly compensated for their data.B. They are built on technological progress made by a third-party organization.C. They violate data sharing agreements in many jurisdictions.D. They usurp a person's likeness and can then be weaponized against them.
answers.definition: They usurp a person's likeness and can then be weaponized against them.

answers.term: Why are anonymization and pseudonymization insufficient protection measures against breaches of data privacy and security?A. They don't integrate well into data science and machine learning workflows.B. They only work in scenarios with particular kinds of personal information.C. They destroy the usefulness of the data.D. They can be broken by combining this data with other publicly available data.
answers.definition: They can be broken by combining this data with other publicly available data.

answers.term: Which of the following are ways that regulations differ from ethical frameworks? (Select two.)A. Regulations provide a clear basis for potential litigation.B. Regulations have legal enforcement behind them.C. Regulations are flexible in their implementation.D. Regulations are often industry led.
answers.definition: Regulations provide a clear basis for potential litigation.  B. Regulations have legal enforcement behind them.

answers.term: Your business handles the personal data of California residents. Which of the following regulations would enable a resident to request that their data be deleted from your company's files? | CCPA | PCI DSS | OECD Privacy Guidelines | COPPA

Which of the following does the Brazilian General Data Protection Act (LGPD) mandate? (Select two.)A. Data protection auditsB. Data protection analystsC. Data protection officersD. Data protection impact assessments
answers.definition: Data protection officers  D. Data protection impact assessments

answers.term: Which of the following is a standard or regulation that focuses on ensuring the implementation of strong cybersecurity techniques like network security and cryptography to protect data?A. PCI DSSB. PIPEDAC. POPID. FERPA

Which of the following are requirements set forth by the Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA)? (Select two.)A. Organizations must obtain consent from individuals regarding the collection and use of biometric data.B. Organizations must store biometric data in local, on-premises databases.C. Organizations must destroy biometric data in a timely fashion.D. Organizations must not transmit biometric data across an unsecured network like the Internet.
answers.definition: Organizations must obtain consent from individuals regarding the collection and use of biometric data.  C. Organizations must destroy biometric data in a timely fashion.

answers.term: The Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) safeguards the privacy of which age group's personal information? | Anyone under 13 years old | Anyone under 18 years old | Anyone between 13 and 18 years old | Anyone between 5 and 13 years old

Which of the following are advantages to adopting standards frameworks like ISO 27000? (Select two.)A. Formal certification processes that provide competitive advantageB. Regulatory weight and legal enforcementC. Technology-specific focus and precise implementation instructionsD. International support, recognition, and involvement
answers.definition: Formal certification processes that provide competitive advantage  D. International support, recognition, and involvement

answers.term: Which of the following is a notable aspect of the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA) when compared to similar laws and regulations?A. Its exclusive focus on a single domain rather than a breadth of domainsB. Its nationwide scope and specific national focusC. A stipulation to continue providing service even if data usage is deniedD. The early date of its inauguration
answers.definition: A stipulation to continue providing service even if data usage is denied

answers.term: Which of the following resources does the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) provide to organizations?A. Industrial configurationsB. Measurement technologiesC. Reference materialsD. Security tools
Which of the following ethical domains does the IEEE 7000 series explore? (Select two.)A. Machine-readable privacy termsB. Fair competitionC. Emulated empathyD. Personnel safety
answers.definition: Machine-readable privacy terms  C. Emulated empathy

answers.term: Which of the following are important elements of the data minimization principle? (Select two.)A. Only delete data that can be easily replacedB. Only collect data that is strictly necessaryC. Only compress data that needs to be kept as small as possibleD. Only keep data for as long as it is needed
answers.definition: Only collect data that is strictly necessary  D. Only keep data for as long as it is needed

answers.term: Which of the following are logical arguments in favor of an organization maintaining compliance? (Select two.)A. Long-term cost savings due to avoiding finesB. Reduced time to deploymentC. Reduced costs of developmentD. Avoidance of reputational damage
answers.definition: Long-term cost savings due to avoiding fines  D. Avoidance of reputational damage

answers.term: How does increasing AI performance often conflict with the desire for explainability?A. Increasing AI performance sometimes reduces the transparency of input data used in training, making it more difficult to explain decision-making processes.B. Increasing AI performance sometimes leads to certain evaluation metrics no longer being useful, making it more difficult to explain decision-making processes.C. Increasing AI performance sometimes leads to greater model complexity, making it more difficult to explain decision-making processes.D. Increasing AI performance sometimes removes human-in-the-loop (HITL) methods, making it more difficult to explain decision-making processes.
answers.definition: Increasing AI performance sometimes leads to greater model complexity, making it more difficult to explain decision-making processes.

answers.term: Which of the following explains why efficiency can sometimes incur systemic fragility?A. High-efficiency machines often require more maintenanceB. Increased efficiency tends to compound over timeC. Efficiency benefits may lead to complex second-order costsD. Increased efficiency tends to create cost savings
answers.definition: Efficiency benefits may lead to complex second-order costs

answers.term: Which of the following are possible benefits of a human-in-the-loop (HITL) architecture? (Select two.)A. Improving the speed of autonomous decision makingB. Eliminating the potential for human error in decision makingC. Balancing the negative effects of an AI system on people with the effects on environments and objectsD. Mitigating excessive scope or potential collateral damage
answers.definition: Balancing the negative effects of an AI system on people with the effects on environments and objects  D. Mitigating excessive scope or potential collateral damage

answers.term: How does the "virtuous cycle" that benefits Big Tech operate? | Better classes of customers lead to richer and more refined data for algorithmic systems. | Data-driven algorithms improve solutions, leading to new customers, and better data. | Organizations write algorithms with fewer biases, which leads to fairer outcomes. | By acting virtuous, the public respects Big Tech more and more.
answers.definition: Data-driven algorithms improve solutions, leading to new customers, and better data.

answers.term: Which of the following is often in opposition to moral relativism?A. Customs and conventionsB. Evidence-based policyC. Subjective perspectivesD. Cultural mores

Which of the following are important aspects of resolving complex and confounding business pressures? (Select two.)A. Managing expectations that not everyone can get what they want, when they want itB. Prioritizing ethical and safety concerns over business desires in all cases and situationsC. Assuring everyone that their desires can be accommodated without compromiseD. Engaging with multiple stakeholders to understand their particular needs
answers.definition: Managing expectations that not everyone can get what they want, when they want it  D. Engaging with multiple stakeholders to understand their particular needs

answers.term: You plan on streamlining your company's product experience, but you also want to uphold the agency and autonomy of your users. Which of the following actions would uphold these principles? (Select two.) | Refraining from guiding users into something they didn't wish for or intend | Applying machine intelligence to simulate customer behavior | Respecting the right of the user to choose and customize their experiences | Enabling government agencies to have a personalized interface with software
answers.definition: Refraining from guiding users into something they didn't wish for or intend | Respecting the right of the user to choose and customize their experiences

answers.term: Which of the following describe corporate hegemony? (Select two.)A. Consolidating interests through mergers and acquisitionsB. Locking out smaller players, leading to monopolies or cartelsC. Spending large sums on corporate branding and marketingD. Making multiple investments in a similar space to improve the outcomes of success
answers.definition: Consolidating interests through mergers and acquisitions  B. Locking out smaller players, leading to monopolies or cartels

answers.term: Which of the following are tasks in the overall risk management process? (Select three.)A. MitigationB. DeploymentC. IdentificationD. EliminationE. Analysis

Which of the following risk analysis methods use words like "likely," "unlikely," and "rare" to describe the likelihood of risk, and words like "low," "medium," and "high" to describe the impact of risk? (Select two.) | Semi-qualitative analysis | Qualitative analysis | Quantitative analysis | Semi-quantitative analysis

What does the attribution data suggest if only the Facebook ad is getting credit? |The budget for Facebook should be reduced in future campaigns|YouTube and Instagram ads did not reach the intended audience|The model may be underestimating the impact of earlier touchpoints|Upper-funnel ads are automatically excluded from attribution analysis
answers.definition: The model may be underestimating the impact of earlier touchpoints

answers.term: radio, A marketing team wants to track app purchases, website sales, and in-store transactions in one reporting system. Which tools should they use to capture these data sources on Meta? |Dynamic creative and lookalike audience tools|Meta Pixel, SDK, and Conversions API|Split testing tools and campaign budget optimization|Meta Ads Library and boosted post reports
answers.definition: Meta Pixel, SDK, and Conversions API

answers.term: radio, A marketer finishes an A/B test that identifies a clear winning ad version. What should they do next to continue improving campaign performance? |Apply the same ad settings to all future campaigns without testing|Pause all testing and wait for quarterly review results|Use the winning version as the new baseline and run another test|Duplicate the ad and change the budget only
answers.definition: Use the winning version as the new baseline and run another test

answers.term: radio, An analyst asks how Media Mix Modeling determines the value of each marketing channel. What should the analyst be told about how this method works? |It gathers real-time performance metrics from recent online campaigns|It uses historical data and regression models to estimate each channel's influence on results|It compares cost-per-click and click-through rates across platforms|It identifies audience preferences through direct customer interviews
answers.definition: It uses historical data and regression models to estimate each channel's influence on results

answers.term: radio, A brand is deciding which rule-based attribution model to apply for analyzing its recent multi-platform campaign. Which of the following is an example of a rule-based attribution model? |Statistical model that uses machine learning to estimate lift per channel|Time-decay attribution model that gives more credit to recent touchpoints|Randomized A/B test with equal exposure to both versions|CRM segmentation model that groups customers by demographic
answers.definition: Time-decay attribution model that gives more credit to recent touchpoints

answers.term: radio, A digital marketing analyst is reviewing options for assigning credit to ad touchpoints along the customer journey. Which attribution model credits the last ad a user clicked before converting? |Time-decay attribution model|Last-click attribution model|First-touch attribution model|Even-credit attribution model

radio, An analyst is reviewing attribution results for a brand awareness campaign. The data shows strong impact from early impressions. What model would best reflect this influence? |First-touch attribution model|Time-decay attribution model|Even-credit attribution model|Last-click attribution model

radio, A business runs ads on social media, their website, and physical stores. Why is tracking online and offline sales important when measuring marketing effectiveness? |To ensure the same creative assets are used consistently|To automate campaign adjustments in real time across platforms|To get a complete view of how all campaigns contribute to overall performance|To comply with platform-based performance benchmarks
answers.definition: To get a complete view of how all campaigns contribute to overall performance

answers.term: radio, A marketing director is reviewing a campaign's annual performance across TV, Facebook, and YouTube. They want to understand which channel contributed most to sales. Which approach would help them determine the contribution of each channel to the final results? |Check which platform had the highest number of impressions|Launch a new A/B test on one platform|Use Media Mix Modeling to analyze past data and evaluate each channel's ROI|Use survey results from customers
answers.definition: Use Media Mix Modeling to analyze past data and evaluate each channel's ROI

answers.term: radio, An advertiser collects data from their app, website, and retail store, but finds it difficult to attribute all actions to a single user. What makes it hard to connect these touchpoints? |Delayed shipment reports from e-commerce vendors|Insufficient ad creative testing across campaigns|Reliance on cookies, which are ineffective across mobile and apps|Misaligned budget allocation across departments
answers.definition: Reliance on cookies, which are ineffective across mobile and apps

answers.term: radio, A social media team wants to run an A/B test comparing two ad headlines. To ensure the test delivers reliable insights, what is one best practice they should follow? |Launch all variations across different campaigns simultaneously|Use as many creative elements as possible to explore new ideas|Test only one variable at a time|End the test as soon as early results favor one version
answers.definition: Test only one variable at a time

answers.term: radio, A marketing team uses available performance data to identify which ads had the greatest incremental impact on conversions. What is a key feature of statistical attribution models? |They automatically duplicate high-performing ad sets|They rely on a pre-selected rule to determine credit assignment|They prioritize the first and last ads by default|They assign fractional credit to touchpoints based on estimated incremental impact
answers.definition: They assign fractional credit to touchpoints based on estimated incremental impact

answers.term: radio, After running an A/B test, a marketing analyst sees that the two versions performed similarly and no confidence level is reported. What does this outcome suggest? |There was no clear winner, and a new test should be created|The campaign's budget was automatically reallocated|The losing version still received partial credit for impressions|A default winner is selected based on audience engagement
answers.definition: There was no clear winner, and a new test should be created

answers.term: radio, A media planner receives attribution data showing high ROI for search and social ads, but low ROI for display ads. What is the most strategic response? |Keep budget allocations the same to maintain consistency|Reallocate budget to channels with higher ROI for the next quarter|Use last-click attribution to reevaluate all results|Pause all campaigns and restart with new creative assets
answers.definition: Reallocate budget to channels with higher ROI for the next quarter

answers.term: radio, A team learns from an A/B test that a specific image outperformed others in generating link clicks. How can this insight be used to improve future campaigns? |Stop testing once a strong image has been identified|Base all future campaigns on the same demographic target|Only use images from the same photoshoot in the next campaign|Apply the insight to new ad creatives and continue testing variations
answers.definition: Apply the insight to new ad creatives and continue testing variations

answers.term: radio, Which of the following outlines the key components of an effective campaign presentation? |Goals, key data, insights and recommended actions|Timeline, creative versions and total spend|Metrics overview and campaign summary|Campaign setup, budget and ad creatives
answers.definition: Goals, key data, insights and recommended actions

answers.term: radio, What is the most effective way to use storytelling in your campaign presentation? |Present data separately from insights|Start with the most impressive data point and work backward|Connect goals to actions, results and future recommendations|Include all metrics to demonstrate thoroughness
answers.definition: Connect goals to actions, results and future recommendations

answers.term: radio, Why is it essential to include both results and insights in a campaign presentation? |Results show performance, while insights explain what the results mean and what to do next|Insights are included to reduce the number of slides focused on data|Results are usually inaccurate, so insights help fill in the gaps|Stakeholders prefer stories over numbers, so insights are more important than results
answers.definition: Results show performance, while insights explain what the results mean and what to do next

answers.term: radio, What is the role of data visualization in campaign presentations? |To make the presentation look more creative and engaging|To display as much data as possible on a single slide|To replace written insights with graphic elements|To clearly communicate key results and trends in an easily understandable format
answers.definition: To clearly communicate key results and trends in an easily understandable format

answers.term: radio, A presenter is sharing their latest campaign results with a leadership team and starts by explaining their campaign goals. Why is it important to begin a presentation this way? |It impresses the audience with how much work was done|It replaces the need to present their campaign's budget|It sets the context for understanding the results and actions taken|It avoids the need to explain their metrics later
answers.definition: It sets the context for understanding the results and actions taken

answers.term: radio, A marketing analyst is building a chart to show how different audiences responded to an ad campaign, but the chart is overcrowded with labels and numbers. What should be done to make the chart easier to understand? |Add multiple data labels for every element of the chart|Leave the chart as-is, since more data makes it look more important|Change the chart type to a 3D graph without adjusting the data|Simplify the chart by removing unnecessary details and focusing on key comparisons
answers.definition: Simplify the chart by removing unnecessary details and focusing on key comparisons

answers.term: radio, An A/B test shows that an ad featuring a person using the product outperformed a simple product image. How should this insight be used going forward? |Use the more engaging ad creative in future campaigns and continue testing other options|Ignore the A/B test results since it was only one test|Change the ad targeting without adjusting the creative|Stop using ads that feature people in them
answers.definition: Use the more engaging ad creative in future campaigns and continue testing other options

answers.term: radio, A campaign team is designing presentation slides and wants to avoid overwhelming the audience. How should slides be used effectively? |Include every possible chart and graph on a single slide for efficiency|Make their slides colorful and animated, even if it distracts from the message|Use short bullet points or keywords to highlight their spoken points|Fill their slides with complete paragraphs so the audience can read everything
answers.definition: Use short bullet points or keywords to highlight their spoken points

answers.term: radio, A marketer feels nervous before starting and wants to center themselves. What technique could help provide calm and focus before speaking? |Take a deep breath or sip water as a calming anchor before starting|Skip practicing and hope for the best|Start talking as fast as possible to finish sooner|Stand silently and wait for someone to prompt them to speak
answers.definition: Take a deep breath or sip water as a calming anchor before starting

answers.term: radio, A team member preparing for a presentation wants to ensure there's a backup plan for accessing the presentation files. What is a good approach to take? |Bring their presentation on a USB drive as a backup option|Only save the presentation on their laptop|Store their presentation in one place and hope it works|Ask someone else to bring the presentation without checking with them
answers.definition: Bring their presentation on a USB drive as a backup option

answers.term: radio, A campaign aimed to increase website subscriptions, but the presentation only includes impressions and reach data. What key mistake is being made when choosing the metrics? |Avoiding technical explanations of their Ads Manager settings|Focusing too much on financial reporting|Including too much conversion data|Presenting metrics that don't align with their campaign goal of conversions
answers.definition: Presenting metrics that don't align with their campaign goal of conversions

answers.term: radio, A campaign's data reveals that most conversions happened on weekends rather than weekdays. How should this insight be used in the next campaign? |Keep the same schedule without changes|Adjust the campaign schedule to focus more on weekends, when performance is stronger|Stop running ads on weekends to try something different|Only focus on adding more creative variations, not scheduling
answers.definition: Adjust the campaign schedule to focus more on weekends, when performance is stronger

answers.term: radio, A marketing analyst is presenting campaign data and wants to help the audience easily compare actual results to campaign goals. What is the best way to make this comparison clear in the chart? |Arrange the data so that each actual result is displayed directly next to its goal|Hide the goal data to focus attention on the results|Use several unrelated charts to show each data point individually|Place the goals and results on separate slides to avoid confusion
answers.definition: Arrange the data so that each actual result is displayed directly next to its goal

answers.term: radio, A marketing campaign team wants to show that their results were carefully tested before sharing conclusions. What could be mentioned to explain the process? |Describe any experiments, such as an A/B test, that were used to validate the results|Focus only on the creative elements of the ads|Avoid explaining their analysis because it might confuse people|Only show the final numbers without describing how they were calculated
answers.definition: Describe any experiments, such as an A/B test, that were used to validate the results

answers.term: radio, A marketing team is presenting campaign results and wants to help the audience evaluate success. What role do campaign goals play in this part of the presentation? |They allow them to avoid answering questions during the presentation|They replace the need to mention key audience segments|They provide a baseline for measuring whether the results met expectations|They remove the need to discuss the campaign's return on ad spend
answers.definition: They provide a baseline for measuring whether the results met expectations

answers.term: radio, A campaign team is preparing a performance presentation and wants the audience to notice the key metric first. What is the best way to help the audience focus on what matters? |Fill the chart with extra decorative elements|Use color contrast to highlight the most critical data point|Add every available metric to the slide|Use a table instead of a chart, even if the audience struggles to read it
answers.definition: Use color contrast to highlight the most critical data point

answers.term: radio, A presenter is starting a presentation on a recent ad campaign and wants to capture the audience's interest immediately. What is the best way to open the presentation? |List every metric the campaign generated before providing context|Start with a rhetorical question, a story or an interesting fact related to their findings|Open by reading the entire slide word-for-word|Begin by reviewing the presentation software they used to make their slides
answers.definition: Start with a rhetorical question, a story or an interesting fact related to their findings

answers.term: radio, A marketing team preparing for a campaign presentation wants to feel confident about the timing and flow. What should be done before presenting? |Practice the entire presentation out loud and time how long it takes|Prepare by reading the slides silently the night before|Skip practice to avoid feeling more nervous|Leave out the opening and conclusion to be as concise as possible
answers.definition: Practice the entire presentation out loud and time how long it takes

answers.term: radio, A campaign aimed to drive sales includes both conversions and return on ad spend (ROAS) in the final presentation. Why is it important to include ROAS? |ROAS hides the actual results and focuses only on budget|ROAS shows how effectively the campaign generated revenue compared to what was spent|ROAS replaces the need to talk about conversions entirely|ROAS only applies to awareness campaigns
answers.definition: ROAS shows how effectively the campaign generated revenue compared to what was spent

answers.term: radio, An A/B test reveals that one creative performed significantly better than the other. What conclusion should be drawn from this data? |Ignore the results because it was only one test|Switch to a completely different campaign objective without analyzing the creative|Use the better-performing creative for future campaigns and continue testing other options|Focus only on changing the budget, not the creative
answers.definition: Use the better-performing creative for future campaigns and continue testing other options

answers.term: radio, A chart showing sales growth starts the vertical axis at 100 instead of 0, making the growth appear larger than it really is. What adjustment should be made? |Leave the axis starting at 100 to make the results appear stronger|Adjust the axis to start at zero so the visual accurately reflects the change in data|Remove the axis entirely so the audience won't question the chart|Add a pie chart next to the bar chart to confuse the audience
answers.definition: Adjust the axis to start at zero so the visual accurately reflects the change in data

answers.term: radio, A team is presenting campaign results that show a clear trend over several months. What is the best chart type to help the audience see how the numbers changed over time? |A line graph, because it clearly shows changes and trends over time|A bar chart, because it hides differences between categories|A table, because it makes it harder to spot patterns|A pie chart, because it shows what the total results look like
answers.definition: A line graph, because it clearly shows changes and trends over time

answers.term: radio, A campaign's results show that women aged 35-44 responded more strongly to the ads than other groups. How should this insight be applied when planning future campaigns? |Focus on campaign cost only and ignore audience results|Keep the same audience targeting without changes|Remove this demographic from targeting to test new audiences|Adjust future targeting to focus more on this high-performing demographic
answers.definition: Adjust future targeting to focus more on this high-performing demographic

answers.term: radio, A social media marketer is worried about looking stiff or awkward while speaking. What is one way to prepare body language in advance? |Avoid moving at all and grip the podium tightly|Use constant hand gestures to fill space and appear energetic|Walk around randomly during the presentation to stay loose|Practice deliberate movements, like stepping forward at key points
answers.definition: Practice deliberate movements, like stepping forward at key points

answers.term: radio, A marketing coordinator is preparing to present in a conference room they haven't used before. What should be done in advance to avoid technical issues? |Wait until the presentation starts to figure out the setup|Bring only a printed copy of their slides and no digital version|Check how to load their presentation on the room's computer or screen|Assume the room will have the correct software
answers.definition: Check how to load their presentation on the room's computer or screen

answers.term: radio, A sales campaign presentation discusses return on ad spend (ROAS). How should this metric be described to the audience? |Say ROAS represents the number of clicks on the campaign|Explain that ROAS shows how much revenue the campaign earned compared to what was spent|Describe ROAS as the total number of people who saw the ads|Skip explaining ROAS because it is too technical for the audience
answers.definition: Explain that ROAS shows how much revenue the campaign earned compared to what was spent

answers.term: radio, When performing logistic regression on sentiment analysis, you represented each tweet as a vector of ones and zeros. However your model did not work well. Your training cost was reasonable, but your testing cost was just not acceptable. What could be a possible reason? |The vector representations are sparse and therefore it is much harder for your model to learn anything that could generalize well to the test set.|You probably need to increase your vocabulary size because it seems like you have very little features.|Logistic regression does not work for sentiment analysis, and therefore you should be looking at other models.|Sparse representations require a good amount of training time so you should train your model for longer
answers.definition: The vector representations are sparse and therefore it is much harder for your model to learn anything that could generalize well to the test set.

answers.definition: Lays out the approach and method for delivering information effectively and efficiently.

Capture a description of the developer's concern in the issue log

answers.definition: Have change thresholds that are appropriate for the type of change.

answers.term: A key stakeholder has been resistant to the project's objectives, and the support of this stakeholder is vital to the success of the project. Perform an alternatives analysis

Implement an online tool to enable the team members to chat among themselves B. Enroll the project team members in cultural training to raise cultural awareness C. Nothing; the business world has been multicultural for so long that there should be no issues D. Funnel all communications through the project manager to avoid miscommunication
answers.definition: Enroll the project team members in cultural training to raise cultural awareness

The project manager should not have included the schedule baseline in the change request. D. The project manager used contingency reserves instead of management reserves.
answers.definition: The project manager used contingency reserves instead of management reserves.

answers.definition: Research various levels of resource capability and skills, types, and sizes
